summary: Target-level plan of the Dwork pencil and general exponent data, specialized monodromy, determinants, local Hodge theory and switching for the selected zero-shaped asymmetric and self-dual systems. General-character ordinarity remains conditional on maximal nilpotence and consecutive labelled weights. All 81 targets are specified; ten explicit proof/supplier gaps and pending upstream imports remain. This is a reviewed mathematical plan, not a claim of formalization or of completed proofs.

nodes.title: Pseudo-reflections and transvections
nodes.statement: Let K be a field and V a K-vector space of finite dimension n ≥ 1. An element g ∈ GL(V) is a pseudo-reflection if g − 1 has rank exactly one, equivalently ker(g − 1) is a hyperplane. It is a transvection if moreover (g − 1)² = 0, equivalently g = 1 + v ⊗ φ for a nonzero v ∈ V and a nonzero φ ∈ V* with φ(v) = 0; equivalently g is a unipotent pseudo-reflection. A pseudo-reflection that is not a transvection is diagonalisable with eigenvalue det g ≠ 1 on a line and 1 on a hyperplane. For a subgroup G ⊆ GL(V), 'generated by transvections' means generated by its elements that are transvections.
hypotheses: Rank is taken over K; for a field extension K′/K, g is a pseudo-reflection (resp. transvection) over K iff it is one over K′.
The identity is neither a pseudo-reflection nor a transvection.
proofSteps: rank(g − 1) = 1 gives g − 1 = v ⊗ φ with v, φ nonzero; then (g − 1)² = φ(v)·(g − 1), so g is unipotent iff φ(v) = 0, and otherwise g has eigenvalue 1 + φ(v) = det g on v.
The characteristic polynomial of a pseudo-reflection is (X − 1)^{n−1}(X − det g); a transvection has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n and determinant 1.

Conjugation, inversion and extension of scalars preserve both notions; Mathlib's elementary matrix Matrix.transvection i j c (i ≠ j, c ≠ 0) is a transvection in this sense, and SL_n(K) is generated by such matrices (Gaussian elimination, Matrix.Pivot.exists_list_transvec_mul_diagonal_mul_list_transvec). The diagonal determinant-one factor is also a product of elementary transvections: reduce to diag(a,a⁻¹), which is the product w(a)w(−1), where w(a) = E₁₂(a)E₂₁(−a⁻¹)E₁₂(a). The n = 1 group SL₁ is trivial.
acceptance: diag(1, …, 1, a) with a ≠ 0, 1 is a pseudo-reflection and not a transvection; the 2 × 2 matrix [[1, 1], [0, 1]] is a transvection.

sources.match: Defines a transvection as a unipotent element whose fixed space has dimension n − 1, and asserts that the local monodromy at t′ = 1 is one.
Uses that the residual monodromy is generated by elements with characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n and fixed space of dimension at least n − 1, i.e. by transvections.
The relation γ_0γ_1γ_∞ = 1 with γ_1 acting by a pseudo-reflection is the input of Levelt's theorem.

nodes.title: Rank-one difference of companion matrices
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, n ≥ 1, and p,q ∈ K[X] distinct monic polynomials of degree n with p(0) ≠ 0. Use the companion matrices supplied by ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.2, with ones on the subdiagonal and the negatives of the coefficients in the last column. Then C(q)C(p)⁻¹ fixes e₂,…,e_n and rank(C(q)C(p)⁻¹−1)=1. The already supplied cyclicity and minimal-polynomial statements imply that C((X−1)^n) is a single unipotent Jordan block; those are imports rather than new targets here.
hypotheses: Orientation as in QIAN23 Lemma 3.4 and BLGHT11 Corollary 4.4, which agrees with CA.2's convention.
proofSteps: For 1 ≤ i < n, C(p)⁻¹e_{i+1}=e_i, so C(q)C(p)⁻¹e_{i+1}=e_{i+1}.
The displacement has at most one nonzero column and is nonzero because p ≠ q, hence has rank one.
For subsequent applications import minpoly C(p)=p from CA.2; a degree-n minimal polynomial (X−1)^n gives one Jordan block. Levelt below constructs its needed basis directly.
acceptance: C((X − 1)²) = [[0, −1], [1, 2]] is conjugate to [[1, 1], [0, 1]] and not to the identity.
For p = (X − 1)² and q = (X − 2)(X − 4) over ℚ, C(q)C(p)^{−1} − 1 has rank one.

nodes.title: Levelt's rigidity theorem for hypergeometric triples
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, n ≥ 1, and α_1, …, α_n, β_1, …, β_n ∈ K̄^× with α_j ≠ β_k for all j, k; put p = ∏(X − α_j), q = ∏(X − β_j), assumed to lie in K[X]. Let A = C(p) and B = C(q) be the companion matrices. If h_0, h_∞ ∈ GL_n(K) satisfy: h_∞ has characteristic polynomial p, h_0^{−1} has characteristic polynomial q, and h_1 := h_0^{−1}h_∞^{−1} is a pseudo-reflection, then there is g ∈ GL_n(K) with gh_∞g^{−1} = A and gh_0g^{−1} = B^{−1}, hence gh_1g^{−1} = BA^{−1}. Conversely (h_0, h_∞) = (B^{−1}, A) satisfies the hypotheses. In particular a triple (h_0, h_1, h_∞) with h_0h_1h_∞ = 1, h_1 a pseudo-reflection and prescribed characteristic polynomials of h_0 and h_∞ with no common root of p and q is unique up to simultaneous conjugation.
hypotheses: α_j ≠ β_k for all j, k (no common eigenvalue of h_∞ and h_0^{−1})
h_1 = h_0^{−1}h_∞^{−1} is a pseudo-reflection (DM.0/pseudo-reflection)
proofSteps: The case n=1 is immediate. For n≥2 put X=h_∞ and Y=h_0⁻¹. Since Y=h_1X, X−Y=(1−h_1)X has rank one. Set W=ker(X−Y).
The intersection W ∩ X^{−1}W ∩ ⋯ ∩ X^{−(n−2)}W is nonzero; pick e ≠ 0 in it, so that X^je ∈ W, hence X^{j+1}e = YX^je, for 0 ≤ j ≤ n − 2.

If e,Xe,…,X^{n−1}e are dependent, take the first dependence at degree d≤n−1. Then U=span(e,…,X^{d−1}e) is a nonzero X-stable subspace contained in W. Hence Y=X on U and U is also Y-stable. Their common restriction has an eigenvalue over K̄, contrary to the disjoint spectra. Thus the vectors form a basis.
In this basis X is the companion matrix of its characteristic polynomial p and Y the companion matrix of q (both act as the shift on the first n − 1 basis vectors), which is the claim.
Uniqueness up to conjugacy follows because both triples are conjugate to (B^{−1}, BA^{−1}, A).
acceptance: n = 1: with h_∞ = α and h_0 = β^{−1}, h_1 = βα^{−1} is a pseudo-reflection of the line exactly when α ≠ β, and g = 1 conjugates the pair to (C(X − β)^{−1}, C(X − α)).
For p = (X − 1)^n and q = ∏_{b∈B}(X − ζ_N^{−b}) the theorem identifies the Dwork monodromy (QIAN23 Lemma 3.4).

The written linear-algebra proof extends the result to any field with disjoint spectra over its algebraic closure.

nodes.title: Irreducibility of hypergeometric groups
nodes.statement: Let K be a field and h_0, h_1, h_∞ ∈ GL_n(K) with h_0h_1h_∞ = 1 and h_1 a pseudo-reflection. If h_∞ and h_0^{−1} have no common eigenvalue in K̄, then the subgroup ⟨h_0, h_∞⟩ acts absolutely irreducibly on K^n.
hypotheses: h_0h_1h_∞ = 1 with h_1 a pseudo-reflection
h_∞ and h_0^{−1} have no common eigenvalue in an algebraic closure of K
proofSteps: Work over K̄. Let 0 ≠ U ⊊ K̄^n be stable under h_0 and h_∞, hence under h_1. The image of h_1 − 1 is a line L.
If L ⊆ U, then h_1 acts trivially on K̄^n/U; otherwise (h_1 − 1)U ⊆ U ∩ L = 0 and h_1 acts trivially on U.
On the piece (U or K̄^n/U) where h_1 acts trivially, h_0h_∞ = 1, so h_∞ and h_0^{−1} agree there and share an eigenvalue: contradiction.
acceptance: For n = 2, K = 𝔽_7, h_∞ = C((X − 1)²) and h_0 = C((X − 2)(X − 4))^{−1}, the group ⟨h_0, h_∞⟩ has no invariant line.

nodes.title: Finite unitary groups
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field, ℓ/k its quadratic extension with Galois generator c, and for M ∈ M_n(ℓ) assume n ≥ 1 and put M† = (M^c)ᵀ. The general unitary group is GU_n(ℓ) = {M ∈ GL_n(ℓ) : M†M = ν(M)·1 for some ν(M) ∈ k^×}, with multiplier character ν : GU_n(ℓ) → k^×. The unitary group is U_n(ℓ) = ker ν and the special unitary group is SU_n(ℓ) = U_n(ℓ) ∩ SL_n(ℓ). For a finite field k′ of even degree over 𝔽_l with σ its automorphism of order two, SU(n, k′) = {g ∈ SL_n(k′) : σ(g)ᵀg = 1} is SU_n(k′) for the quadratic extension k′/k′^σ. Give ℓ its star operation c. U and SU use Mathlib Matrix.unitaryGroup and Matrix.specialUnitaryGroup; this node adds GU and the finite-field compatibility and order results, rather than redefining those carriers.
hypotheses: BCGNT25 Definition 4.3.1 writes SU_n(ℓ) for ker ν; the groups used afterwards (Proposition 4.4.2, Lemma 5.2.3) are U_n(ℓ) ∩ SL_n(ℓ), as here (sourceIssue PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII/E1).
n ≥ 1 makes the scalar multiplier unique; at n=0 every scalar satisfies the matrix equation, so it does not define a multiplier function.
proofSteps: M ↦ M† is an anti-automorphism of M_n(ℓ) with (AB)† = B†A† and M†† = M; so GU_n(ℓ) is a subgroup and ν is a homomorphism.
For M ∈ GU_n(ℓ), N_{ℓ/k}(det M) = ν(M)^n; hence det maps U_n(ℓ) onto the norm-one subgroup of ℓ^× (onto by Hilbert 90 applied to diagonal matrices) and SU_n(ℓ) has index q + 1 in U_n(ℓ), q = #k.
Changing the Hermitian form by an equivalence conjugates these groups inside GL_n(ℓ) (DM.0/hermitian-forms-unique).
acceptance: #U_1(𝔽_9) = 4 (the norm-one elements of 𝔽_9^×) and SU_1(𝔽_9) is trivial.

nodes.title: Hermitian and skew-Hermitian forms over a quadratic extension
nodes.statement: Let ℓ/k be a quadratic extension of fields with nontrivial automorphism c, and V a finite-dimensional ℓ-vector space. A Hermitian form on V is a k-bilinear map ⟨·,·⟩ : V × V → ℓ with ⟨ax, y⟩ = a⟨x, y⟩, ⟨x, ay⟩ = c(a)⟨x, y⟩ for a ∈ ℓ, and ⟨y, x⟩ = c(⟨x, y⟩). It is skew-Hermitian if instead ⟨y, x⟩ = −c(⟨x, y⟩). Nondegenerate means that x ↦ ⟨x, ·⟩ is injective. Multiplying by η ∈ ℓ^× with c(η) = −η interchanges Hermitian and skew-Hermitian forms. The isometry group of ⟨·,·⟩ and its similitude group (isometries up to a scalar in k^×) are defined as usual; for the standard form ⟨x, y⟩ = ∑ x_i c(y_i) they are U_n(ℓ) and GU_n(ℓ).
hypotheses: Bilinearity is over k; the form is ℓ-linear in the first and c-semilinear in the second variable (BCGNT25 convention).
Use the linear-first convention. In coordinates put Aᵢⱼ=B(e_j,e_i), so B(x,y)=y†Ax. For a multiplier function assume B nondegenerate and dim V ≥ 1; arbitrary forms still have an isometry group.
proofSteps: Hermitian forms are the sesquilinear forms for the ring involution c whose Gram matrix satisfies A† = A.
For η ≠ 0 with c(η)=−η, scaling and cancelling η identifies Hermitian forms and skew-Hermitian forms; the zero scalar does not give an equivalence.
Similitudes preserve products and inverses; nondegeneracy on a nonzero space gives a pair with B(x,y) ≠ 0 and hence uniqueness and multiplicativity of the multiplier.
acceptance: On ℓ = 𝔽_9 ⊃ k = 𝔽_3, ⟨x, y⟩ = x c(y) = x y³ is a nondegenerate Hermitian form on ℓ.

sources.match: Defines Hermitian forms for a quadratic extension of finite fields and observes that scaling by an element of trace zero gives the skew version.
The pairings on the level-structure data are Hermitian up to such a scalar.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of nondegenerate Hermitian forms over finite fields
nodes.statement: Let ℓ/k be a quadratic extension of finite fields and V an ℓ-vector space of dimension n. Every nondegenerate Hermitian form on V has an orthonormal basis; hence any two nondegenerate Hermitian forms on V are isometric, and the isometry group of any of them is conjugate in GL(V) to U_n(ℓ) (and its similitude group to GU_n(ℓ)).
hypotheses: k finite (surjectivity of the norm ℓ^× → k^× is used)
proofSteps: A nonzero Hermitian form has an anisotropic vector: if ⟨x, x⟩ = 0 for all x, polarisation ⟨x + ay, x + ay⟩ = Tr_{ℓ/k}(c(a)⟨x, y⟩) for all a forces ⟨x, y⟩ = 0, using surjectivity of the trace. This also works in characteristic two: the trace of a nonzero scalar multiple cannot vanish on all ℓ because the finite extension is separable.
For x with ⟨x, x⟩ = d ∈ k^×, choose a ∈ ℓ^× with N(a) = d^{−1} (the norm of finite fields is surjective) and replace x by ax, of length 1.
Split off the line and induct on the orthogonal complement, which is nondegenerate.
acceptance: On 𝔽₉=𝔽₃[i], i²=−1, one has N(i)=1 and N(1+i)=−1. Thus scaling the second basis vector by 1+i identifies diag(1,1) with diag(1,−1).

sources.match: Uses that there is a unique equivalence class of nondegenerate Hermitian forms for a quadratic extension of finite fields, citing Lewis §4.

nodes.title: Conjugate self-dual absolutely irreducible representations are unitary
nodes.statement: Let ℓ/k be a quadratic extension of finite fields with generator c, G a group, V an ℓ-vector space of dimension n with an absolutely irreducible representation of G, and χ : G → k^× a character. If there is an ℓ-linear G-isomorphism V^∨ ≅ V^c ⊗ χ^{−1}, then V carries a nondegenerate G-invariant-up-to-χ Hermitian form, unique up to k^×-scaling, and in a suitable basis the representation takes values in GU_n(ℓ) with multiplier χ.
hypotheses: V absolutely irreducible
the isomorphism V^∨ ≅ V^c ⊗ χ^{−1} is ℓ-linear and G-equivariant
χ takes values in k^×
proofSteps: The isomorphism is a nondegenerate G-equivariant pairing ψ : V × V^c → χ; by Schur's lemma it is unique up to ℓ^×.
ψ′(x, y^c) := c(ψ(y, x^c)) is another such pairing, so ψ′ = λψ; applying twice gives N_{ℓ/k}(λ) = 1.
By Hilbert 90, λ = c(η)/η; rescaling ψ by η^{−1} gives a Hermitian form ⟨x, y⟩ = ψ(x, y^c) with ⟨gx, gy⟩ = χ(g)⟨x, y⟩.
By DM.0/hermitian-forms-unique choose an orthonormal basis; then G lands in GU_n(ℓ) with multiplier χ.
acceptance: For n = 1 and G acting on ℓ through a character θ with θ·c(θ) = χ, the conclusion is that θ takes values in the norm-χ elements.

sources.match: States and proves that a conjugate self-dual absolutely irreducible representation over a finite field is unitary, via Schur's lemma, Hilbert 90 and uniqueness of Hermitian forms.

nodes.title: Normal subgroups of SL_n and SU_n over finite fields
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field of characteristic l > 2 with q elements and n ≥ 2. (1) SL_n(k) is perfect, its centre is the group μ_n(k) of scalar matrices, every proper normal subgroup is central, and PSL_n(k) = SL_n(k)/μ_n(k) is a nonabelian simple group, except for (n, q) = (2, 3). (2) For the quadratic extension ℓ/k and n ≥ 3, SU_n(ℓ) is perfect, its centre consists of the scalars of SU_n(ℓ), every proper normal subgroup is central, and PSU_n(ℓ) is a nonabelian simple group (n ≥ 3, q odd). (3) Consequently the composition factors of SL_n(k) (resp. SU_n(ℓ)) are PSL_n(k) (resp. PSU_n(ℓ)) and cyclic groups of order dividing n, every nontrivial quotient has PSL_n(k) (resp. PSU_n(ℓ)) as a composition factor, and these groups have no nontrivial abelian quotient.
hypotheses: l odd (the exceptional small cases (2, 2), (2, 3), (3, 2) for SU_3 are excluded or have even characteristic)
n ≥ 2 for SL_n, n ≥ 3 for SU_n
In part (3), exclude (n,q)=(2,3) for SL, as in part (1). The small symplectic exception is treated separately in DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy.
proofSteps: SL_n(k) is generated by transvections (DM.0/pseudo-reflection) and acts primitively on lines of k^n; the stabiliser of a line contains the abelian normal subgroup of transvections with that centre, whose conjugates generate SL_n(k); perfectness for (n, q) ≠ (2, 2), (2, 3) follows from commutators of transvections; Iwasawa's criterion (Mathlib MulAction.IwasawaStructure.isSimpleGroup) gives simplicity of PSL_n(k). The rank-two case is Mathlib's Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.rank_two_simple.

For SU_n use its primitive action on isotropic lines and the long-root subgroup in the centre of the corresponding unipotent radical. That centre is abelian and normal in the line stabiliser; the whole radical is generally not abelian. The required generation and perfectness statements are the finite unitary input cited in BCGNT25 Lemma 5.2.3; their detailed root-group proof remains an explicit DM.0 closure input, rather than being asserted to follow from matrix notation alone.
The centre of SL_n(k) is the scalars by Mathlib Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.center_equiv_rootsOfUnity; a central quotient is cyclic of order dividing n, which gives (3).
acceptance: PSL_3(𝔽_3) is simple of order 5616; SL_2(𝔽_3) is not perfect (its abelianisation has order 3), which is why (2, 3) is excluded.

sources.match: Uses that the cyclic composition factors of SL_n(k(λ)) have order dividing n and that every nontrivial quotient of SL_n over a field of characteristic > 10 has PSL_n as a composition factor.
States perfectness of SL_n and SU_n in the relevant range and simplicity of PSL_n and PSU_n, used in Proposition 4.4.2.
The symplectic analogue: the only cyclic composition factors of Sp_n(𝔽_{l^r}) have order 2 or 3, and PSp_n is simple outside Sp_2(𝔽_3).

nodes.title: Simple linear groups in different characteristics are not isomorphic
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and let l_1 ≠ l_2 be odd primes with max(l_1, l_2) > 10, and let k_1, k_2 be finite fields of characteristics l_1, l_2. Then PSL_n(k_1) is not isomorphic to PSL_n(k_2) or to PSU_n(k_2′) (k_2′/k_2 quadratic, n ≥ 3), PSU_n(k₁′) is also not isomorphic to PSU_n(k₂′) for n≥3; and likewise with the roles reversed; and PSp_n(k_1) ≇ PSp_n(k_2) for n even. Consequently no composition factor of SL_n(k_2) or SU_n(k_2′) is isomorphic to PSL_n(k_1) or PSU_n(k_1′).
hypotheses: l_1, l_2 odd and distinct
max(l_1, l_2) > 10 excludes the coincidences in small characteristic (e.g. PSL_2(𝔽_4) ≅ PSL_2(𝔽_5), PSL_2(𝔽_7) ≅ PSL_3(𝔽_2))
proofSteps: Use only the restricted cross-characteristic non-isomorphism statements in Qian’s product proof, BLGHT Corollary 4.8 (symplectic case), and BCGNT Lemma 5.2.3 (the same-rank linear and unitary cases). The hypothesis max(l₁,l₂)>10 excludes their small cross-characteristic coincidences. Do not assert that order determines every finite Lie-type group: there are same-order type B/C cases outside this statement. Verification of the original Artin list and a complete elementary order-comparison proof remain in the finite-group gap.
The second statement follows from DM.0/special-linear-unitary-simple(3): the noncyclic composition factor of SL_n(k_2) is PSL_n(k_2).
acceptance: PSL_2(𝔽_{11}) (order 660) is not isomorphic to PSL_2(𝔽_{3^r}) for any r, since 660 is not of the form 3^r(3^{2r} − 1)/2.

sources.match: Excludes an isomorphism between quotients of SL_n over fields of different characteristics, one of them > 10, citing Artin's theorem on the orders of classical simple groups.

nodes.title: Irreducible groups generated by transvections (Zalesskii–Serezhkin), in the form used
nodes.statement: Let l be an odd prime, n > 2 and k′ a finite field of characteristic l. Let G ⊆ GL_n(k′) be an absolutely irreducible subgroup generated by transvections. Then G is conjugate in GL_n(k′) to SL_n(k), Sp_n(k) or SU(n, k) (DM.0/finite-unitary-group) for some subfield k ⊆ k′ (Sp_n only for n even, SU(n, k) only for [k : 𝔽_l] even). The statement is false for n = 2 (SL_2(𝔽_5) ⊂ SL_2(𝔽_9) is generated by its elements of order 3, which are transvections).
hypotheses: l odd
G absolutely irreducible and generated by transvections
proofSteps: Apply precisely the odd-characteristic, dimension >2 case of Zalesskii–Serezhkin: the absolutely irreducible transvection-generated group is special linear, symplectic, or unitary over a subfield. The exceptional binary icosahedral subgroup in characteristic 3 has dimension 2 and is excluded by n>2. No order-N exclusion is part of this argument.
acceptance: For n = 2 the conclusion fails: SL_2(𝔽_5) embeds in SL_2(𝔽_9) as an absolutely irreducible subgroup generated by transvections that is none of SL_2(k), SU(2, k).

sources.match: Applies the main theorem of Zalesskii–Serezhkin to the residual monodromy, generated by transvections, to obtain SL_n(k), Sp_n(k) or SU(n, k) for a subfield k.
The same classification for the self-dual family.

nodes.title: Surjectivity onto a product of two groups with distinct simple quotients
nodes.statement: Let H₁,H₂ be finite groups. Assume every nontrivial quotient of H₁ has a composition factor isomorphic to a fixed nonabelian simple group S₁, and no composition factor of H₂ is isomorphic to S₁. If Γ≤H₁×H₂ surjects onto both factors, then Γ=H₁×H₂. The same result holds after interchanging the factors. H₂ need not be perfect, so the statement also applies to the small solvable symplectic factor Sp₂(𝔽₃).
hypotheses: Γ projects onto H_1 and onto H_2
proofSteps: By Goursat's lemma (Mathlib Subgroup.goursat) Γ is the preimage of the graph of an isomorphism H_1/N_1 ≅ H_2/N_2 for normal subgroups N_i.
If N_1 ≠ H_1, then H_1/N_1 has S_1 as a composition factor, but H_1/N_1 ≅ H_2/N_2 has only composition factors of H_2: contradiction. Hence N_1 = H_1, N_2 = H_2 and Γ = H_1 × H_2.
acceptance: For H_1 = SL_3(𝔽_{13}) and H_2 = SL_3(𝔽_{3^r}) every subgroup of H_1 × H_2 surjecting on both factors is everything.

nodes.title: Auxiliary moduli with prescribed order of l
nodes.statement: Let l be a prime, s ≥ 1 an integer and S a finite set of primes. There is a positive integer N, divisible by no prime of S ∪ {l}, such that the order r of l in (ℤ/Nℤ)^× is divisible by s and, when r is even, N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1. Since every prime below a given bound may be put into S, N may be taken larger than any given bound, and N may be taken odd and prime to any given integer. In particular (BLGHT11 Lemma 6.1) for every m ≥ 1 there is such an N with m | r, so that every finite field of characteristic l and degree dividing m embeds in 𝔽_l(ζ_N).
hypotheses: l is prime, s ≥ 1, and every member of S is prime. The construction works for l=2 as well as for odd l.
proofSteps: Write s=2ᵃ∏pᵢ^{aᵢ}. For a sufficiently large t, choose odd prime factors A of l^{2^{t−2}}+1 and B of l^{2^{t−1}}+1 outside S. Their orders are 2^{t−1} and 2ᵗ. For l odd each displayed integer is 2 mod 4, and for l=2 both are odd, so such odd factors exist. Increasing t excludes the finite set S by comparing the orders of l modulo its members.
Set M₀=AB. Its order is 2ᵗ, while l^{2^{t−1}} is 1 modulo A and −1 modulo B; thus −1 does not lie in the cyclic subgroup generated by l modulo M₀.

For each odd pᵢ choose tᵢ≥aᵢ large enough. The cyclotomic value Φ_{pᵢ}(l^{pᵢ^{tᵢ−1}}) exceeds pᵢ. Any prime divisor belonging to the current finite exclusion set must be pᵢ, and it occurs to valuation one (expand the geometric sum modulo pᵢ²). Hence there is a new odd prime Mᵢ outside that set whose order for l is exactly pᵢ^{tᵢ}. This is an elementary valuation argument, not an appeal to an unplanned primitive-divisor theorem.

Take N=M₀∏Mᵢ. The Chinese remainder theorem gives order 2ᵗ∏pᵢ^{tᵢ}, divisible by s. Its half-power is 1 modulo A, so cannot equal −1 modulo N. Adding all primes below a bound to S forces N above that bound.
acceptance: A prime N never satisfies both conditions with r even, since then l^{r/2} ≡ −1 mod N; for l = 3 and s = 4 the composite N = 35 works: r = lcm(4, 6) = 12 and 3^6 ≡ 29 ≢ −1 mod 35.

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, Lemma2.3 with proof, pp.8–9; opening §4, p.21

nodes.title: The Dwork pencil of hypersurfaces
nodes.statement: Let N ≥ 3 be an odd integer. Over T_0 = ℙ¹ − ({∞} ∪ μ_N) over ℤ[1/N] (coordinate t; equivalently T_0 = Spec ℤ[1/N][t, (1 − t^N)^{−1}]), let Y ⊂ ℙ^{N−1} × T_0 be the hypersurface X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N = N t X_1⋯X_N and π : Y → T_0 the projection. Then π is smooth and projective of relative dimension N − 2 with geometrically connected fibres; the fibre Y_0 is the Fermat hypersurface of degree N, and over t ∈ μ_N the fibre acquires N^{N−2} ordinary double points (the H_0-orbit of (1 : ⋯ : 1) when t = 1). Write Y_s for the fibre at a point s.
hypotheses: N odd (so that N − 2 is odd and the fibres have odd dimension)
N invertible on the base
proofSteps: Partial derivatives N X_i^{N−1} − N t ∏_{j≠i} X_j vanish simultaneously only if X_i^N = t∏_j X_j for all i; summing gives the equation, and multiplying gives t^N = 1 once all X_i ≠ 0; if some X_i = 0 then all vanish. So Y is smooth over the locus t^N ≠ 1 where N is invertible.
At t = 1 the singular points are the H_0-translates of (1 : ⋯ : 1), with Hessian N(N·I − J) on the tangent space, nondegenerate: ordinary double points.
A hypersurface of dimension ≥ 1 in projective space is connected, and smooth fibres are geometrically integral.
acceptance: For N = 3, Y is the Hesse pencil X_1³ + X_2³ + X_3³ = 3tX_1X_2X_3 of plane cubics, smooth exactly for t³ ≠ 1.

sources.match: Defines T_0, the family X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N = NtX_1⋯X_N and asserts smoothness of relative dimension N − 2.
The same family for the self-dual case, with the automorphism ς.
The family Z over T_0 = Spec R_0[t, (1 − t^N)^{−1}], R_0 = ℤ[ζ_N, N^{−1}].

nodes.title: Symmetry groups of the Dwork pencil and their characters
nodes.statement: Let H = μ_N^N/μ_N (diagonal μ_N) and H_0 = {(ξ_1, …, ξ_N) : ξ_1⋯ξ_N = 1}/μ_N ⊂ H. Over ℤ[1/N, ζ_N], H acts on Y by (ξ_i)·(X_i, t) = (ξ_iX_i, (∏ξ_i)^{−1}t); thus H_0 acts on every fibre Y_s over T_0 and H acts on Y_0. For integers a_1, …, a_N with ∑a_i ≡ 0 mod N, ξ ↦ ∏ξ_i^{a_i} is a well-defined character H → μ_N (its restriction to H_0 depends only on (a_i) modulo adding a constant vector). After fixing ζ_N, Hom(H, μ_N) ≅ ker(∑ : (ℤ/Nℤ)^N → ℤ/Nℤ). In addition, the involution ς : X_j ↦ X_{N+1−j} of Y normalises H_0. For a character χ of H_0 and a coefficient ring R in which #H_0 = N^{N−2} is invertible and which contains the values of χ, the idempotent e_χ = (1/#H_0)∑_{ξ∈H_0} χ(ξ)^{−1}ξ cuts out the χ-isotypic part of any R[H_0]-module.
hypotheses: N invertible on the coefficients for the idempotent
the action of H on t is through ∏ξ_i^{−1}, so only H_0 acts fibrewise
proofSteps: The formula preserves the equation, since ∏(ξ_iX_i) = (∏ξ_i)∏X_i is compensated by t ↦ (∏ξ_i)^{−1}t, and the diagonal μ_N acts trivially on ℙ^{N−1} and on t because ζ^N = 1.
Characters of μ_N^N trivial on the diagonal are the exponent vectors with ∑a_i ≡ 0; restricting to H_0 kills exactly the constant vectors.
e_χ is an idempotent of R[H_0] projecting onto the χ-isotypic part because #H_0 is a unit in R.
acceptance: For N = 3, H_0 ≅ μ_3 (one generator (ζ, ζ^{−1}, 1)), acting on the Hesse pencil fibrewise.

nodes.title: Exponent data and the complementary index set
nodes.statement: Fix 2 ≤ n ≤ N and an odd N ≥ 3 prime to n. A Dwork exponent datum is a vector a = (a_1, …, a_N) ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^N with ∑a_i = 0 such that the residues a_j take exactly N − n distinct values. Its index set is B(a) = {b ∈ ℤ/Nℤ : b + a_j ≠ 0 for all j}, of cardinality n, and its character is χ_a|_{H_0}. Two data are equivalent if they differ by a permutation and a constant vector (same character on H_0 up to permutation of coordinates). The two families used are: Qian's asymmetric data for n > 2 (0 occurring n + 1 times, every nonzero residue at most once, with the explicit vectors of QIAN23 p. 1253: for n odd B = {1, 2, N − 3} ∪ {(N + x)/2 : x = −n + 4, −n + 6, …, n − 4}; for n even B = {1, 2, 3, N − 6} ∪ {(N + x)/2 : x = −n + 5, …, n − 5}); and the self-dual data of BLGHT11 (n even, a = (1, 2, …, (N − n − 1)/2, 0, …, 0, (N + n + 1)/2, …, N − 1) with n + 1 zeros), whose index set is B = {(N + 1 − n)/2, …, (N − 1 + n)/2} = −B. For n = 2 Qian's datum is the self-dual one with B = {(N − 1)/2, (N + 1)/2}. For these two selected families, 0 ∉ B and ∑_{b∈B}b=0. Neither conclusion follows for arbitrary exponent data. Call a chosen representative zero-shaped if zero occurs n+1 times and each nonzero exponent occurs at most once. This extra condition is used for the one-block hypergeometric comparison and consecutive Hodge numbers, rather than being inferred from rank n.
hypotheses: N odd, gcd(N, n) = 1; Qian's explicit vectors need N > 100n + 100 (the stabiliser lemma) and n > 2
proofSteps: b ∉ B iff −b is one of the N − n values of the a_j, so #B = n.
If 0 occurs among the a_j then 0 ∉ B; the explicit vectors list their values, from which B is read off.
∑B ≡ −(sum of the distinct values not taken) and the explicit choices make this 0; for the self-dual datum B = −B gives ∑B = 0 directly.

nodes.title: Trivial multiplicative stabiliser of Qian's index set
nodes.statement: Let n > 2 and N odd with N > 100n + 100 and gcd(N, n) = 1, and let B ⊂ ℤ/Nℤ be the index set of Qian's asymmetric datum. If α ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^× satisfies αB = B, then α = 1. In particular −B ≠ B, and l^jB ≠ B, l^jB ≠ −B for every power l^j ≢ 1 (resp. ≢ −1) mod N. For n = 2 (and for the self-dual data) B = −B.
hypotheses: N odd, N > 100n + 100, gcd(N, n) = 1
proofSteps: 1 ∈ B, so α ∈ B. The small elements 1, 2 (and 3 for n even) and the large element N − 3 (resp. N − 6) are isolated from the middle block {(N + x)/2}, because N > 100n + 100.
α = 2 would force 4 ∈ B, α = N − 3 would force 9 or −9 into B, and similarly for 3 and N − 6; none of these lie in B.

If α = (N + x)/2 lies in the middle block, then 2α = x ∈ B forces x ∈ {1, 3} (n even) or {1, −3} (n odd); then (N − x)/2 ∈ B too and their product −x²/4 ∈ B, so 4B contains −1 or −9, which the explicit description of 4B excludes.
acceptance: n = 3, N = 401: multiplication by 2 sends B = {1, 2, 398} to {2, 4, 395} ≠ B.

nodes.title: The quotient family over the thrice-punctured line
nodes.statement: Let T′_0 = ℙ¹ − {0, 1, ∞} with coordinate t′. For n > 2 let Y′ ⊂ ℙ^{N−1} × T′_0 be X′_1^N + ⋯ + X′_{N−1}^N + t′^{−1}X′_N^N = N X′_1⋯X′_N, with H_0 acting by scaling coordinates. The map t ↦ t′ = t^N is a Galois covering T_0 − {0} → T′_0 with group μ_N, and X′_i = X_i (i < N), X′_N = tX_N identify its pullback of Y′ with Y − Y_0, H_0-equivariantly. For the self-dual datum (BLGHT11), the family Ỹ with t′^{−1} placed on the middle coordinate X̃_{(N+1)/2}, which is stable under ς̃ : X̃_j ↦ X̃_{N+1−j}, plays the same role. Over ℚ(ζ_N), Ỹ is the quotient of Y − Y_0 by the copy of μ_N acting on the middle coordinate.
hypotheses: n > 2 for Y′ (for n = 2 use Ỹ, since Y′ is not ς-stable)
proofSteps: Substituting X′_N = tX_N gives t′^{−1}t^NX_N^N = X_N^N and N X′_1⋯X′_N = N t X_1⋯X_N, so the pullback equation is that of Y.
The deck transformation t ↦ ζt lifts to Y − Y_0 through the element of H acting on X_N (resp. on X_{(N+1)/2}); this identifies the quotient.
H_0 commutes with the identification because it scales the X_i without changing t.
acceptance: For N = 3 and the Hesse pencil, t′ = t³ and Y′ is X_1³ + X_2³ + t′^{−1}X_3³ = 3X_1X_2X_3.

nodes.title: Cohomology of the Fermat hypersurface
nodes.statement: Let X ⊂ ℙ^{N−1} be the Fermat hypersurface ∑X_i^N = 0 over a field of characteristic 0 or prime to N containing μ_N, with the action of H = μ_N^N/μ_N. For a character a = (a_1, …, a_N) ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^N, ∑a_i = 0, of H, the a-eigenspace of the primitive middle cohomology H^{N−2}_prim (Betti over ℚ(ζ_N), ℓ-adic over a characteristic-zero coefficient field containing μ_N, or de Rham in characteristic zero) is zero unless every a_i ≠ 0, in which case it is one-dimensional; the remaining cohomology in degree N − 2 is the a = 0 part (spanned by a power of the hyperplane class, zero for N − 2 odd). Over ℂ, the a-eigenline (all a_i ≠ 0, representatives ⟨a_i⟩ ∈ {1, …, N − 1}) lies in H^{p, N−2−p} with p + 1 = ∑_i⟨a_i⟩/N.
hypotheses: N invertible on the coefficients and on the base field
μ_N in the coefficients (for eigenspaces)

For the integral coefficient versions assert finite projective rank-one eigensummands; freeness is automatic after completion at λ or reduction modulo a nonzero ideal, but is not inferred over a global Dedekind ring merely from being a direct summand. The de Rham Hodge statement is in characteristic zero.

Take the cohomological left action of a geometric automorphism h to be (h⁻¹)*. With the resulting exponent labels, the Hodge degree is p=∑⟨aᵢ⟩/N−1, as in Deligne §7. A change to h* inverts all character labels.
proofSteps: X is the quotient-free cover of ℙ^{N−2} branched along a hyperplane arrangement, and its cohomology decomposes under H; the dimension count of eigenspaces comes from the Lefschetz trace formula for elements of H (or from the explicit description of X as a μ_N^{N−1}-cover of ℙ^{N−2}).
The Hodge type of an eigenline is computed by Griffiths' residue description of H^{N−2}_prim with the monomial forms X^{b−1}Ω/F^k (Deligne, Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, §7).
acceptance: N = 3: the characters with all a_i ≠ 0 and ∑a_i ≡ 0 mod 3 are (1, 1, 1) and (2, 2, 2), so H¹ of the Fermat cubic curve has rank 2; ∑⟨a_i⟩/3 = 1 and 2 put the two eigenlines in H^{0,1} and H^{1,0}.

sources.locator: Updated author chapter (1 October 2018), §7, Propositions7.4 and 7.6, pp.45–48

nodes.title: Integral cohomology of smooth hypersurfaces is torsion-free
nodes.statement: Let X ⊂ ℙ^{m+1}_ℂ be a smooth hypersurface of dimension m. Then H^i(X(ℂ), ℤ) is torsion-free for every i. Consequently, for a smooth proper family of hypersurfaces over a base where ℓ is invertible, the sheaves R^iπ_*ℤ_ℓ are torsion-free and R^iπ_*(ℤ/ℓ^k) = R^iπ_*ℤ_ℓ/ℓ^k.
hypotheses: X smooth hypersurface in projective space
proofSteps: By the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem H^i(X, ℤ) ≅ H^i(ℙ^{m+1}, ℤ) for i < m and H_i(X, ℤ) ≅ H_i(ℙ^{m+1}, ℤ) for i < m, so these are torsion-free; Poincaré duality and the universal coefficient theorem give torsion-freeness in degrees > m and in degree m (torsion of H^m is torsion of H_{m−1}, which vanishes).

Smooth proper base change and the Artin comparison transfer this to the étale sheaves R^iπ_*ℤ_ℓ on any base with ℓ invertible, through a complex fibre; the universal coefficient sequence gives the reduction statement.

For a geometric fibre in positive characteristic, lift the defining smooth hypersurface to a mixed-characteristic DVR by lifting its coefficients. Smoothness is open and properness makes the lifted model smooth after restricting the base. Smooth proper base change and the characteristic-zero comparison transfer the torsion-free calculation; there is no assertion that a positive-characteristic point is itself a complex point.
acceptance: For a smooth plane cubic, H¹(X, ℤ) ≅ ℤ² is torsion-free.

nodes.title: The Dwork eigen-local-systems V_λ, V[𝔫] and V_B
nodes.statement: Let a be a Dwork exponent datum with character χ of H_0, O = ℤ[1/(2N), ζ_N]. (1) For a prime λ of O of residue characteristic l, V_λ = e_χ R^{N−2}π_*O_λ, a lisse étale sheaf of O_λ-modules on T_0 × Spec O[1/l]. (2) For a nonzero ideal 𝔫 of O of norm M, V[𝔫] = e_χ R^{N−2}π_*(O/𝔫), a lisse sheaf of O/𝔫-modules on T_0 × Spec O[1/M]. (3) After fixing τ : ℚ(ζ_N) ↪ ℂ with τ(ζ_N) = e^{2πi/N}, V_B = e_χ R^{N−2}π̃_*O on T_0(ℂ), a local system of O-modules. (4) V′_B on T′_0(ℂ), defined the same way from Y′, pulls back to V_B|_{T_0(ℂ)−{0}}. These are compatible: V_B ⊗ O_λ corresponds to τ*V_λ and V_B ⊗ O/𝔫 to τ*V[𝔫] under the equivalence of locally constant analytic and étale sheaves on (T_0)_ℂ; and V[𝔫] ≅ ∏_λ V_λ/λ^{a_λ} for 𝔫 = ∏λ^{a_λ}. For n = 2 and the self-dual data, U_λ, U[𝔫], U_B denote these sheaves, replaced by the real forms of DM.2/self-dual-real-forms. Stalks are written V_{λ,t}, V[𝔫]_t, V_{B,t}; BCGNT25 writes V_{t,λ} with coefficients O_{M_λ}, M = ℚ(e^{2πi/N}), which is the same object.
hypotheses: #H_0 = N^{N−2} and 2 invertible in O
λ ∤ residue characteristic of the base points used
The chosen action on cohomology is (h⁻¹)*, consistently with the exponent/Hodge convention. Betti stalks over O are finite projective of rank n; the λ-adic and finite coefficient stalks are free.
proofSteps: R^{N−2}π_* of the smooth proper π is lisse with torsion-free stalks (smooth proper base change, DM.2/integral-cohomology-torsion-free); H_0 acts by functoriality and e_χ is an idempotent endomorphism, so its image is a direct summand, again lisse.
The Artin comparison and Ehresmann's theorem identify the analytic and étale local systems on complex fibres; e_χ commutes with them.
Chinese remainder theorem for O/𝔫 and exactness of e_χ give the product decomposition.
acceptance: For the cubic boundary N=3,n=2, χ|H₀ is trivial and the eigenpart has rank 2; the two nontrivial H-characters (1,1,1) and (2,2,2) split the Fermat fibre. Nontrivial H₀-characters have rank zero.

nodes.title: Poincaré duality between conjugate eigensheaves
nodes.statement: The cup product and the trace H^{2N−4}(Y_t) ≅ O(2 − N) restrict to perfect pairings V_{χ,λ} × V_{χ^{−1},λ} → O_λ(2 − N) between the χ- and χ^{−1}-eigensheaves (and likewise with O/𝔫 and Betti coefficients). Since N − 2 is odd the cup product on the middle cohomology is alternating, so the pairing satisfies ⟨y, x⟩ = −⟨x, y⟩ after exchanging the factors. In particular: (1) for the self-dual data (χ = χ^{−1} up to ς) the real forms V_λ carry perfect alternating pairings V_λ × V_λ → O^+_λ(2 − N); (2) complex conjugation c on the coefficients gives c-linear isomorphisms V_{c(λ)} ≅ V_λ^∨(2 − N) for Qian's data.
hypotheses: N odd (alternating middle cup product)
coefficients with 2N invertible
The Hesse cubic illustrates duality for the two inverse characters of H, not for nontrivial characters of H₀: H₀ acts trivially on its H¹.
proofSteps: Poincaré duality for the smooth proper fibres is a perfect pairing on R^{N−2}π_*, alternating since N − 2 is odd, and H_0-invariant.
An invariant pairing pairs the χ-part with the χ^{−1}-part and kills χ-part × χ′-part for χ′ ≠ χ^{−1}; perfectness passes to the eigen-summands.
Composing with the coefficient conjugation, which exchanges χ and χ^{−1} = c ∘ χ, gives the c-linear self-duality.
acceptance: For the Hesse pencil (N = 3) the pairing on H¹ of an elliptic curve pairs the two eigenlines of μ_3.

nodes.title: Real forms of the self-dual Dwork eigensheaves
nodes.statement: For the self-dual datum (n even, BLGHT11) let O^+ = ℤ[1/(2N), ζ_N]^+ and e = (1/(2#H_0))(ς + 1)∑_{ξ∈H_0}(χ(ξ) + χ(ξ)^{−1})ξ in O^+[H_0 ⋊ ⟨ς⟩]. Define V_λ = [e]_*R^{N−2}π_*O^+_λ, V[𝔫] = [e]_*R^{N−2}π_*(O^+/𝔫) and V_B = [e]_*R^{N−2}π̃_*O^+, for λ, 𝔫 of O^+. These are locally free of rank n, carry perfect alternating pairings V_λ((N − 1 − n)/2) × V_λ((N − 1 − n)/2) → O^+_λ(1 − n) (and mod 𝔫), and H_0-equivariant projection gives isomorphisms V_λ ⊗_{O^+} O ≅ U_λ, V[𝔫] ⊗ O ≅ U[𝔫], V_B ⊗ O ≅ U_B with the χ-eigensheaves of DM.2/dwork-eigensheaves. For n = 2, Qian uses these real forms in place of U_λ, U[𝔫], U_B; their residue fields k(λ) are those of O^+.
hypotheses: n even, N odd, N > n + 1
2N invertible (e has denominator 2#H_0 = 2N^{N−2}; for V_B the coefficient ring is O^+ = ℤ[1/(2N), ζ_N]^+, PAPER-QIAN-23/E25)

The Betti stalks are finite projective over O⁺, with free λ-adic and finite coefficient realizations; locally free here is in the coefficient-ring sense. The Hesse boundary N=3,n=2 is excluded by N>n+1.
proofSteps: e is an idempotent of O^+[H_0 ⋊ ⟨ς⟩] since ς normalises H_0 and swaps χ and χ^{−1}; it defines a self-correspondence of Y over T_0 × Spec O^+.
After extending scalars to O, e decomposes into the projections to the χ- and χ^{−1}-parts exchanged by ς, so projection to the χ-part is an isomorphism from the image of e.
The pairing of DM.2/eigensheaf-duality restricted to the image of e is O^+-valued and perfect.
acceptance: For n = 2 the real form V_λ has rank 2 over O^+_λ with a perfect alternating pairing, so its geometric monodromy lies in Sp_2 = SL_2.

nodes.title: Splitting of the Fermat fibre into eigenlines
nodes.statement: Since H acts on Y_0, the fibres at t = 0 decompose as V_{λ,0} = ⊕_{i∈ℤ/Nℤ} V_{λ,i} and V[𝔫]_0 = ⊕ V_i[𝔫], where V_{λ,i} is the part on which H acts by χ_i : ξ ↦ ∏_j ξ_j^{a_j+i} (whose restriction to H_0 is χ). The summand V_{λ,i} is nonzero iff i ∈ B(a), and then it is free of rank one over O_λ (resp. O/𝔫). The corresponding Betti summands are finite projective of rank one over O, and one-dimensional after passing to ℚ(ζ_N); the same splitting holds, for the χ-part of H^{N−2}_dR(Y_0/K) (K ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N)), and for the self-dual real forms (summands U_{i,λ}, (N + 1 − n)/2 ≤ i ≤ (N − 1 + n)/2). For the quotient obtained by rescaling coordinate q, choose the orientation of the monodromy generator at t′=0 so that its action on this line is ζ_N^{a_q+i}. It is ζ_N^i when a_q=0, as for Qian’s last-coordinate choice for n>2 and the middle-coordinate self-dual choice.
hypotheses: Y_0 the Fermat fibre; coefficients contain 1/N and ζ_N
proofSteps: The characters of H restricting to χ on H_0 are the χ_i, i ∈ ℤ/Nℤ.
χ_i has exponent vector (a_j + i)_j, all of whose entries are nonzero iff i ∈ B(a); apply DM.2/fermat-hypersurface-cohomology.
The deck transformation scales the chosen coordinate q. Its value on χ_i is ζ_N^{a_q+i}, up to reversing the peripheral orientation. The zero-coordinate choices give the displayed ζ_N^i formula.
acceptance: For Qian's datum with n = 3, the nonzero summands are V_{λ,1}, V_{λ,2}, V_{λ,N−3}.

sources.match: Decomposes V_{λ,0} and V[𝔫]_0 under H into the χ_i-parts and shows, by DMOS Proposition I.7.4, that they are nonzero, of rank one, exactly for i ∈ B.
U_{i,λ} is free of rank one for (N + 1 − n)/2 ≤ i ≤ (N − 1 + n)/2 and zero otherwise.

nodes.title: The Dwork eigensheaves are locally free of rank n
nodes.statement: For every rank-n Dwork exponent datum, the λ-adic sheaf V_λ and the finite-coefficient sheaf V[𝔫] are lisse with free stalks of rank n over O_λ and O/𝔫. The Betti systems V_B and V′_B have finite projective stalks of constant rank n over O, equivalently stalks locally free as O-modules. After scalar extension to ℚ(ζ_N), completion at λ, or reduction modulo 𝔫 they are free of rank n. The same claims, with O⁺ in place of O, hold for the self-dual real forms. No global O-basis is deduced solely from smoothness and properness.
hypotheses: Torsion-freeness of the integral middle cohomology of the fibres is used (PAPER-QIAN-23/E24).
proofSteps: The sheaves are locally constant (smooth proper base change, Ehresmann) with torsion-free stalks (DM.2/integral-cohomology-torsion-free); a direct summand of a locally constant sheaf of finite free modules is locally free.
The rank is constant on the connected base and equals the rank at t = 0, which is #B = n by DM.2/fermat-fibre-splitting.
For V′_B on T′_0(ℂ), which does not contain the point t = 0, pull back along t ↦ t^N to V_B on T_0(ℂ) − {0} and use connectedness.

A finite projective module over a local ring is free, and O/𝔫 is a finite product of local rings. Over the global Dedekind rings O and O⁺ retain finite projectivity, rather than silently strengthening it to freeness.
acceptance: For Qian's datum with n = 3 the stalk V_{λ,t} is free of rank 3 over O_λ for every t ∈ T_0.

sources.match: States that V_λ, V[𝔫], V_B and V′_B are locally free of rank n, checking the rank on the fibre at 0 with DMOS Proposition I.7.4.
V_λ (resp. V[𝔫]) is locally free of rank n, and V[𝔫] ≅ ∏ V_λ/λ^{a_λ}.

nodes.title: Katz's hypergeometric sheaf attached to a Dwork exponent datum
nodes.statement: Let M = ℚ(e^{2πi/N}), R_0 = ℤ[ζ_N, N^{−1}], T_1 = Spec R_0[x, x^{−1}, (1 − x)^{−1}] with open immersion j : T_1 → 𝔾_{m,R_0} and f : T_1 → 𝔾_m, x ↦ 1 − x. Let n≥1 and let ρ₁,…,ρ_n : μ_N→M× be distinct nontrivial characters. The construction does not require their product to be trivial. For a zero-shaped Dwork datum take the missing characters indexed by B(a), with the Kummer convention fixed by the trace formula below; the selected Qian and self-dual data also satisfy ∏ρ_i=1. For a place λ of M of residue characteristic l, let L_i be the rank-one lisse M_λ-sheaf on 𝔾_{m,R_0}[1/l] attached to ρ_i and the Kummer μ_N-torsor x ↦ x^N, F_i = j_!f^*L_i, and E_λ = j^*(F_1 ∗_! F_2 ∗_! ⋯ ∗_! F_n)[n − 1], where ∗_! is multiplicative convolution with compact support on 𝔾_{m,R_0}[1/l] (A ∗_! B = Rm_!(A ⊠ B) for the multiplication m : 𝔾_m × 𝔾_m → 𝔾_m).
hypotheses: ρ₁,…,ρ_n are distinct and nontrivial, n≥1. The extra condition ∏ρ_i=1 is imposed only for the pure-Tate determinant formula and the selected Dwork applications.
l invertible on the base
proofSteps: L_i is the ρ_i-isotypic part of the pushforward of the constant sheaf along the Kummer cover x ↦ x^N.
Multiplicative convolution with compact support is Rm_! of the external product; it is associative and commutative up to canonical isomorphism.
The shift [n − 1] places the convolution, restricted to T_1, in degree zero (DM.3/hypergeometric-sheaf-properties).
acceptance: n = 1: E_λ = j^*F_1 = L_{ρ_1}(1 − x) restricted to T_1, a Kummer sheaf of rank one.

sources.match: Defines E_λ as the restriction to T_1 of the shifted multiplicative convolution with compact support of the sheaves j_!f^*L_i (the restriction is j^*, as recorded in the extraction's review).

nodes.title: Basic properties of the hypergeometric sheaf
nodes.statement: In the setting of DM.3/katz-hypergeometric-sheaf: (1) E_λ is a lisse M_λ-sheaf of rank n on T_1[1/l]; E_λ ⊗ M̄_λ is geometrically irreducible; E_λ is pure of weight n − 1; and det E_λ ≅ M_λ(n(1 − n)/2) (using ∏ρ_i = 1). (2) For a finite field k with q elements that is an R_0[1/l]-algebra and x ∈ T_1(k), tr(Frob_k | E_{λ,x}) = (−1)^{n−1}∑_{x_1⋯x_n = x}∏_iρ_i((1 − x_i)^{(q−1)/N}), with μ_N identified with k^×[N] and ρ_i(0) = 0.
hypotheses: ρ_i distinct, nontrivial, ∏ρ_i = 1
l invertible
proofSteps: Lisse of rank n, geometric irreducibility and purity are Katz's theorems on hypergeometric sheaves (ESDE Chapter 8) applied to the convolution of the F_i.
The determinant is computed by Katz's determinant formula (ESDE Theorem 8.12.2(1a)), which gives a Tate twist when the product of the characters is trivial.
The trace formula follows from the Lefschetz trace formula for Rm_! and the definition of the F_i.
acceptance: For n=1 and a nontrivial ρ₁, the constructor and trace formula give the Kummer sheaf with trace ρ₁(1−x); this checks the general constructor only. It is outside this theorem’s product-one determinant hypothesis.
For n=2 and (ρ,ρ⁻¹), ρ≠ρ⁻¹ and ρ≠1, the determinant is E(−1), so geometric determinant is trivial and geometric Frobenius has determinant q.

nodes.title: Local monodromy of the hypergeometric sheaf
nodes.statement: In the setting of DM.3/katz-hypergeometric-sheaf, the geometric local monodromy of E_λ ⊗ M̄_λ is: at x = 0, unipotent with a single Jordan block of size n (the n trivial characters at 0); at x = ∞, tame and isomorphic to ⊕_{i=1}^n L_{ρ_i} (the n distinct characters at ∞); at x = 1, a pseudo-reflection.
hypotheses: ρ_i distinct and nontrivial
proofSteps: Katz's description of the local monodromy of a hypergeometric sheaf of type (n, n): at 0 it is ⊕ over the distinct characters of the list at 0 of the Kummer sheaf tensored with a unipotent block whose size is the multiplicity; at ∞ the same for the list at ∞; at 1 it is a pseudo-reflection (ESDE Theorem 8.4.2, cited as Theorem 8.4.11 in BLGHT11).
For E_λ the list at 0 consists of n copies of the trivial character (each F_i is lisse at 0 with trivial local monodromy) and the list at ∞ is ρ_1, …, ρ_n.
acceptance: n = 1: L_{ρ_1}(1 − x) is unramified at 0, has monodromy ρ_1 at ∞ and is a pseudo-reflection (a nontrivial character) at 1.

nodes.title: Katz's comparison of Dwork eigensheaves with hypergeometric sheaves
nodes.statement: Let U=T_0−{0}, j′:U→T_0 and g:U→T_1, t ↦ t^{−N}. For every place λ of M of residue characteristic l there is a unique continuous character Ψ_λ : π_1(Spec R_0[1/l]) → O_{M_λ}^× and an isomorphism of M_λ-sheaves on U[1/l]: (j′)^*V_λ ⊗ M_λ ≅ g^*E_λ ⊗ M_λ(Ψ_λ). Consequently the χ-eigensheaf V′ of the quotient family over T′_0 (DM.1/three-punctured-cover), whose pullback along t ↦ t^N is (j′)^*V_λ, is isomorphic to the pullback of E_λ along t′ ↦ 1/t′, twisted by Ψ_λ and by a Kummer character L_θ of order dividing N.
hypotheses: Qian's exponent datum (or any datum with n + 1 zeros, nonzero residues at most once)
l invertible

U is the punctured Dwork parameter line; T′₀ remains the quotient parameter line with coordinate t′=t^N from DM.1. These are distinct bases. The nonzero exponent multiplicities must be at most one and zero must have multiplicity n+1.
proofSteps: Katz, Another look at the Dwork family, Theorem 5.3: on the complement of μ_d in the affine line, the primitive eigenpiece of a Dwork-type family is the d-th power pullback of a hypergeometric sheaf tensored with a character of π_1 of the base, provided the eigenpiece is nonzero; BCGNT25 specialises it to the present family, using [−1]^*H_can(trivial^n; ρ) ≅ H_can(ρ^{−1}; trivial^n).
Uniqueness of Ψ_λ follows from geometric irreducibility (DM.3/hypergeometric-sheaf-properties) and Schur's lemma.
Two lisse sheaves on T′_0 with isomorphic geometrically irreducible pullbacks along the μ_N-cover t ↦ t^N differ by a character of μ_N (Kummer twist).
acceptance: Ranks agree: both sides have rank n, the rank of V_λ (DM.2/eigensheaf-rank) and of E_λ.

nodes.title: The twisting character comes from an algebraic Hecke character
nodes.statement: There is a Hecke character Ψ : ℚ(ζ_N)^×\𝔸^×_{ℚ(ζ_N)} → ℂ^× of type A_0, unramified away from N, with values of its finite part in M, such that for every λ the character Ψ_λ of DM.3/katz-dwork-comparison is the λ-adic character attached to Ψ. Moreover Ψ·c(Ψ) corresponds to ε^{n+1−N}, so Ψ is pure of weight N − n − 1 (the printed |·|^{N−n} is corrected as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E7; the sign of the exponent depends on the normalisation of the Artin map).
hypotheses: Correction E21: c-linear duality pairs V_{c(λ)} with V_λ∨(2−N).
The recognition step is conditional on the local-algebraicity input in the recorded gap. Do not infer de Rhamness of Ψ from DM.7, which in turn uses this construction.
proofSteps: For almost all places, the Frobenius traces of Ψ_λ are ratios of traces of V_λ and E_λ, which lie in M and are independent of λ (Katz–Messing for V_λ, the trace formula for E_λ); this is Katz's Question 5.5 argument.

Use R24.5/character-system for the converse recognition of finitely ramified algebraic/de Rham rank-one characters. The compatible Frobenius values alone do not check its local algebraicity hypothesis. Prove this hypothesis for the comparison character Ψ_λ, or supply the precise compatible-character version of Henniart used by BCGNT. This is the explicit character-recognition gap; AG2.0’s forward construction alone does not close it.
From the c-linear isomorphisms V_{c(λ)} ≅ V_λ^∨(2 − N) (DM.2/eigensheaf-duality) and E_{c(λ)} ≅ E_λ^∨(1 − n), Schur's lemma gives Ψ_λ·c(Ψ_λ) = ε^{n+1−N}.
acceptance: Weight check: V_λ has weight N − 2 and E_λ weight n − 1, so Ψ has weight (N − 2) − (n − 1) = N − n − 1.

sources.locator: arXiv:2309.15880v3, Lemma4.2.4 and proof, pp.41–42, with E21 and the explicit recognition-hypothesis gap

The traces of the character Λ are expected to be universal; for the invariant part they are ± 1.

nodes.title: The twisted Dwork local systems W_λ
nodes.statement: For a place λ of M of residue characteristic l let W_λ = V_λ ⊗_{O_{M_λ}} O_{M_λ}(Ψ_λ^{−1}), a lisse sheaf of free O_{M_λ}-modules of rank n on T_0[1/l]. Then W_λ ⊗ M_λ is pure of weight n − 1, geometrically irreducible, with determinant M_λ(n(1 − n)/2). Write W_{t,λ} for its stalk at t, W̄_λ = W_λ ⊗ k(λ) and W̄_{t,λ} likewise. The family {W_λ} has λ-independent Frobenius traces with values in M.
hypotheses: Qian's exponent datum, n > 2 (BCGNT25 setting); Ψ from DM.3/twisting-hecke-character
proofSteps: Twisting by the character Ψ_λ^{−1} of π_1(Spec R_0[1/l]) changes neither lisseness nor geometric monodromy.

On U=T₀−{0}, DM.3/katz-dwork-comparison gives W_λ⊗M_λ≅g*E_λ with g(t)=t⁻ᴺ:U→T₁. Thus purity and determinant follow from the hypergeometric properties, and irreducibility follows by the finite cyclic restriction argument below. Since U is dense open in the smooth connected T₀, π₁(U)→π₁(T₀) is surjective, so this also proves geometric irreducibility on T₀.

For geometric irreducibility after the finite cyclic pullback, first use semisimplicity for the pure sheaf and Clifford theory: isotypic pieces of the restriction to a normal finite-index subgroup are permuted transitively. A power of the monodromy at x=0 is still a single unipotent block. Its invariant decomposition forces one isotypic piece and multiplicity one, so the restriction is irreducible. Irreducibility does not follow merely by pulling back an irreducible sheaf along a finite cover.
acceptance: det W_λ ≅ M_λ(n(1 − n)/2), so the Hodge–Tate weights of any fibre sum to n(n − 1)/2.

sources.match: Defines W_λ = V_λ ⊗ O_{M_λ}(Ψ_λ^{−1}) and records that it is pure of weight n − 1, geometrically irreducible, with determinant M_λ(n(1 − n)/2).

nodes.title: The Dwork monodromy representations and peripheral loops
nodes.statement: Fix τ : ℚ(ζ_N) ↪ ℂ with τ(ζ_N) = e^{2πi/N}, a base point t ∈ T_0(ℂ) − {0} and t′ = t^N ∈ T′_0(ℂ). Let ρ_t : π_1(T_0(ℂ), t) → GL(V_{B,t}) and ρ_{t′} : π_1(T′_0(ℂ), t′) → GL(V′_{B,t′}) be the monodromy representations, with V′_{B,t′} = V_{B,t}. Choose loops γ_0, γ_1, γ_∞ around 0, 1, ∞ generating π_1(T′_0(ℂ), t′) freely on two of them, with the single relation γ_0γ_1γ_∞ = 1, and orient γ_0 so that its image in the deck group of T_0(ℂ) − {0} → T′_0(ℂ) is e^{2πi/N} = τ(ζ_N). On the index-N normal subgroup π_1(T_0(ℂ) − {0}, t), ρ_{t′} restricts to ρ_t composed with π_1(T_0(ℂ) − {0}, t) ↠ π_1(T_0(ℂ), t). For λ a prime of O (of O^+ for the real forms), ρ̄_t and ρ̄_{t′} denote the reductions on V_{B,t}/λ.
hypotheses: Self-dual data: the same with BLGHT11's Ṽ_B on T̃_0 = T′_0
proofSteps: The local system V′_B gives ρ_{t′}; the identification of its pullback with V_B|_{T_0(ℂ)−{0}} (DM.2/dwork-eigensheaves) gives the restriction statement.

π_1 of the thrice-punctured sphere is free on two peripheral loops with the product relation (Tau Ceti BelyiMaps, layer 5); the covering t ↦ t^N corresponds to the kernel of the map to ℤ/N sending γ_0 ↦ 1, γ_1 ↦ 0.

BelyiMaps §5.6 uses p₁p₀p_∞=1 with p*q=q.trans p. To use the convention γ₀γ₁γ_∞=1 here, take γ₀=p₀, γ₁=p₀⁻¹p₁p₀ and γ_∞=p_∞. This only conjugates a peripheral generator. Carry this change of basis through the hypergeometric triple and its monodromy representation.
acceptance: ρ_{t′}(γ_0)^N lies in the image of ρ_t (it is the monodromy of V_B around t = 0, which is trivial since V_B is lisse at 0).

nodes.title: Monodromy at zero: eigenvalues ζ_N^b, b ∈ B
nodes.statement: ρ_{t′}(γ_0) has characteristic polynomial ∏_{b∈B}(X − ζ_N^b), with distinct roots; in particular det ρ_{t′}(γ_0) = ζ_N^{∑B} = 1. For the self-dual data, ρ_et(γ_0) has characteristic polynomial ∏_{j=(N−n+1)/2}^{(N+n−1)/2}(X − ζ_N^j).
hypotheses: γ_0 oriented as in DM.4/dwork-monodromy-representations

Use the selected Qian data with a_N=0, or the middle-coordinate self-dual quotient with zero exponent. For a general quotient coordinate q the eigenvalues are ζ_N^{a_q+b}, and determinant one need not hold.
proofSteps: γ_0 acts on V′_{B,t′} as the deck transformation ζ_N acts on the fibre of V_B at 0, by parallel transport to t = 0 inside T_0(ℂ).
On the eigenline V_{B,i} (i ∈ B) this is multiplication by ζ_N^i (DM.2/fermat-fibre-splitting).
acceptance: n = 3, N = 401: ρ_{t′}(γ_0) has eigenvalues ζ, ζ², ζ^{398}.

nodes.title: Monodromy at one: Picard–Lefschetz
nodes.statement: ρ_{t′}(γ_1) is unipotent with (ρ_{t′}(γ_1) − 1)² = 0 and ρ_{t′}(γ_1) − 1 of rank at most one (a transvection once it is nontrivial). More precisely: the fibre Y_1 has N^{N−2} ordinary double points forming one free H_0-orbit; with Δ the set of vanishing cycles (one per singular point, permuted by H_0 up to sign) the monodromy T around t = 1 on H^{N−2}(Y_t(ℂ), ℤ) is x ↦ x + ε∑_{δ∈Δ}⟨x, δ⟩δ (ε = ±1 depending on N); since N − 2 is odd, the cup product is alternating and vanishing cycles at distinct points are orthogonal, so (T − 1)² = 0; on the χ-part, T − 1 has image in the line spanned by ∑_{ξ∈H_0}χ(ξ)^{−1}ξδ_0. This node proves unipotence, (T − 1)² = 0 and rank(ρ_{t′}(γ_1) − 1) ≤ 1; that the rank is exactly one is proved in DM.4/companion-model-of-monodromy, after the monodromy at ∞ is known. For the self-dual data the same argument gives characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n and dim ker(ρ(γ_1) − 1) ≥ n − 1.
hypotheses: N odd
t′ ↦ t^N étale near t = 1, so ρ_{t′}(γ_1) is conjugate to the restriction of T
proofSteps: Locate the singular points of Y_1 (DM.1/dwork-pencil) and apply the Picard–Lefschetz formula for ordinary double points in a proper family over a disc (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.2, complex comparison and odd relative dimension).
H_0 commutes with the monodromy and permutes Δ up to sign, so on the χ-eigenpart the variation factors through one functional x ↦ ⟨x, δ_0⟩.

Odd fibre dimension makes ⟨δ, δ′⟩ = 0 for all vanishing cycles, so (T − 1)² = 0 on all of H^{N−2}; this replaces BLGHT's symplectic step, which does not apply to the non-self-dual χ-part (PAPER-QIAN-23/E28).
acceptance: For the Hesse pencil (N = 3) the monodromy around t = 1 on H¹ of the elliptic fibre is a transvection with three vanishing cycles permuted by μ_3.

sources.match: Asserts that ρ_{t′}(γ_1) is a transvection, referring to BLGHT11 Lemma 4.3(2).
Picard–Lefschetz theory gives an H_0-orbit Δ of vanishing cycles, the exact sequence and the formula x ↦ x ± ∑⟨x, δ⟩δ, whence ker(γ_1 − 1) has rank ≥ n − 1 on each eigenpart.

nodes.title: Monodromy at infinity is unipotent
nodes.statement: ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) is unipotent, with characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n, and so is the local monodromy of ρ_t around t = ∞ (which is conjugate to ρ_{t′}(γ_∞)^{±N}). This holds for Qian's data and for the self-dual data.
hypotheses: gcd(n, N) = 1
The v1 proof of Qian Lemma3.3(2), pp.13–14, establishes only the unipotence after taking the N-th power; the proof below uses Katz’s comparison (E13).
proofSteps: By DM.3/katz-dwork-comparison, V′ ≅ (pullback of E_λ along t′ ↦ 1/t′) ⊗ Ψ_λ ⊗ L_θ with Ψ_λ geometrically trivial and L_θ a Kummer character of order dividing N. The point t′ = ∞ corresponds to x = 0, where E_λ has unipotent local monodromy with one Jordan block (DM.3/hypergeometric-local-monodromy). Hence ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) = c·u with u unipotent with one Jordan block and c a scalar with c^N = 1 (after the Betti–étale comparison of DM.2/dwork-eigensheaves).

det ρ_{t′}(γ_0) = 1 (DM.4/monodromy-at-zero) and ρ_{t′}(γ_1) is unipotent by the Picard–Lefschetz description (the unipotence part of DM.4/picard-lefschetz-at-one does not use this node), so det ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) = 1 and c^n = 1.
gcd(n, N) = 1 gives c = 1. The local monodromy of V_B at t = ∞ is ρ_{t′}(γ_∞)^{±N}, unipotent; this agrees with the semistable-model argument of QIAN21 Lemma 2.1 and the local monodromy theorem.
acceptance: For the self-dual datum with n = 2, ρ(γ_∞) has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)² and determinant 1.

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, Lemma3.3(2), pp.13–14; the quotient-unipotence proof needs the repair recorded in E13
sources.match: States that ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n; the printed proof via a semistable blowup of the reciprocal family and Illusie's local monodromy theorem yields unipotence only for the N-th power (E27).
Proves the self-dual case from Katz 2009 Theorem 5.3 and Katz ESDE Theorem 8.4.11.
The comparison (4.2.3) with the hypergeometric sheaf, used here for the non-self-dual data.

nodes.title: Companion-matrix model of the Dwork monodromy
nodes.statement: ρ_{t′}(γ_1) − 1 has rank exactly one, so ρ_{t′}(γ_1) is a transvection. Let A and B be the companion matrices of (X − 1)^n and ∏_{b∈B}(X − ζ_N^{−b}), both in GL_n(ℤ[ζ_N]), and ρ : π_1(T′_0(ℂ), t′) → GL_n(ℤ[ζ_N]) the representation γ_0 ↦ B^{−1}, γ_∞ ↦ A, γ_1 ↦ BA^{−1}. Then ρ_{t′} ⊗ ℂ (coefficients extended along τ) is equivalent to ρ ⊗ ℂ, and ρ(γ_1) − 1 has rank one with nonzero entries only in the first column. The same holds for the self-dual data with B the companion matrix of ∏_{j=(N−n+1)/2}^{(N+n−1)/2}(X − ζ_N^j), and then ρ is irreducible (BLGHT11 Corollary 4.4).
hypotheses: Qian's data (n > 2) or the self-dual data
proofSteps: If ρ_{t′}(γ_1) = 1 then ρ_{t′}(γ_0) = ρ_{t′}(γ_∞)^{−1} would have eigenvalue 1, contrary to DM.4/monodromy-at-zero (0 ∉ B) and DM.4/unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity; with DM.4/picard-lefschetz-at-one the rank of ρ_{t′}(γ_1) − 1 is exactly one.

ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n (DM.4/unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity), ρ_{t′}(γ_0)^{−1} has characteristic polynomial ∏(X − ζ_N^{−b}) (DM.4/monodromy-at-zero), with no common root since 0 ∉ B, and ρ_{t′}(γ_1) is a pseudo-reflection (DM.4/picard-lefschetz-at-one).
Levelt's theorem (DM.0/levelt-rigidity) conjugates (ρ_{t′}(γ_0), ρ_{t′}(γ_∞)) to (B^{−1}, A).
BA^{−1} − 1 has rank one by DM.0/companion-normal-form.
acceptance: n = 3: A = C((X − 1)³) has columns e_2, e_3, (1, −3, 3)ᵀ.

The self-dual analogue, with irreducibility from Beukers–Heckman Proposition 3.3.

nodes.title: Maximally unipotent monodromy at infinity
nodes.statement: ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) has minimal polynomial (X − 1)^n: it is a single unipotent Jordan block. Hence the local monodromy of ρ_t around t = ∞, conjugate to ρ_{t′}(γ_∞)^{±N}, is also a single unipotent Jordan block (a nonzero power of a single unipotent Jordan block in characteristic 0 is again one; in positive characteristic a power can split, so this is a statement over ℂ or ℚ̄_l). The same holds for the self-dual family (BLGHT11 Corollary 4.5 and Proposition 4.2(2)) and, by coefficient conjugation, for every Galois conjugate σχ of the character.
hypotheses: characteristic 0 coefficients for the statement about the N-th power
proofSteps: By DM.4/companion-model-of-monodromy, ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) is conjugate to A = C((X − 1)^n), whose minimal polynomial is (X − 1)^n (DM.0/companion-normal-form); alternatively this follows directly from DM.3/hypergeometric-local-monodromy.
If u = 1 + ν with ν nilpotent of order n, then u^m − 1 = mν(1 + …) has the same nilpotency order when m is invertible.
The automorphism σ of the coefficients carries the χ-eigensheaf onto the σχ-eigensheaf compatibly with monodromy (DM.2/dwork-eigensheaves).
acceptance: In the boundary case N = n + 1 = 5 (excluded here, treated in HSBT10), the H_0-invariant part of the Dwork quintic family has a single unipotent Jordan block of size 4 at t = ∞, the classical large complex structure point.

sources.match: ρ_{t′}(γ_∞) has minimal polynomial (X − 1)^n, and so does the monodromy around ∞ under ρ_t.
The self-dual analogue: the monodromy at infinity is unipotent with one Jordan block.

nodes.title: Absolute irreducibility of the residual monodromy
nodes.statement: Let λ be a prime of O (of O^+ for the self-dual data) of odd residue characteristic l ∤ N. Then the reduction ρ̄_{t′} : π_1(T′_0(ℂ), t′) → GL(V′_{B,t′}/λ) is absolutely irreducible and isomorphic to the reduction ρ̄ of the companion representation; ρ̄_{t′}(γ_1) is a transvection, ρ̄_{t′}(γ_∞) is unipotent and ρ̄_{t′}(γ_0) has the n distinct eigenvalues ζ_N^b mod λ, b ∈ B.
hypotheses: l odd and prime to N
λ ∤ N ensures ζ_N^b ≢ 1 mod λ for b ∈ B
proofSteps: Reduce the characteristic polynomials of DM.4/monodromy-at-zero and DM.4/unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity modulo λ; ρ̄_{t′}(γ_1) − 1 has rank ≤ 1, and = 1 since otherwise ρ̄(γ_0) = ρ̄(γ_∞)^{−1} would have eigenvalue 1.
Apply DM.0/hypergeometric-group-irreducible: ρ̄(γ_∞) and ρ̄(γ_0)^{−1} have no common eigenvalue.

Apply Levelt’s theorem directly over the residue field (DM.0/levelt-rigidity). The reduced triple has the two prescribed disjoint spectra and rank-one displacement at 1, so it is simultaneously conjugate to the reduced companion triple. This supplies the actual isomorphism without an unlisted Brauer–Nesbitt input or a claim that integral lattices are conjugate.
acceptance: For n = 3, l = 3, N = 401 the reduction mod a prime above 3 has no invariant line or plane.

sources.match: Shows ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible by the Beukers–Heckman argument and identifies ρ̄_{t′} with it by equality of traces.
The self-dual analogue.

nodes.title: Full special linear residual monodromy
nodes.statement: Let n > 2, Qian's datum, l an odd prime prime to N, λ a prime of O = ℤ[1/(2N), ζ_N] above l, so k(λ) = 𝔽_{l^r} with r the order of l mod N; if r is even assume N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1, equivalently −1 ∉ ⟨l⟩ ⊂ (ℤ/Nℤ)^×. Then ρ̄_{t′}(π_1(T′_0(ℂ), t′)) = SL(V′_{B,t′}/λ) ≅ SL_n(k(λ)) and ρ̄_t(π_1(T_0(ℂ), t)) = SL(V_{B,t}/λ) for every t ∈ T_0(ℂ). Equivalently the geometric monodromy of V[λ] (and of W̄_λ) is SL_n(k(λ)).
hypotheses: N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 when r is even
l odd, l ∤ N
proofSteps: The normal closure Δ of γ_1 has cyclic quotient generated by γ_0 (or γ_∞); the index of ρ̄(Δ) in the image divides both N (order of ρ̄(γ_0)) and a power of l (order of the unipotent ρ̄(γ_∞)), so the image is generated by transvections.
It is absolutely irreducible (DM.4/residual-monodromy-absolutely-irreducible); by DM.0/zalesskii-serezhkin-classification it is conjugate to SL_n(k), Sp_n(k) or SU(n, k) for k ⊆ k(λ).

A proper subfield would make the eigenvalue set {ζ^b} of ρ̄(γ_0) stable under l^m with l^m ≢ 1 mod N, i.e. l^mB = B; Sp_n(k(λ)) would force B = −B; SU(n, k(λ)) would force l^{r/2}B = −B. DM.1/asymmetric-stabiliser-trivial excludes all three, the last with N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1.

π_1(T_0(ℂ) − {0}) is normal of index N in π_1(T′_0(ℂ)), so ρ̄_t has image normal in SL_n(k(λ)) with cyclic quotient of order dividing N; the cyclic composition factors of SL_n(k(λ)) have order dividing n (DM.0/special-linear-unitary-simple) and gcd(N, n) = 1.
acceptance: If l ≡ 1 mod N then k(λ) = 𝔽_l, r = 1 is odd, and the residual monodromy of V[λ] is SL_n(𝔽_l); this is the case of the auxiliary prime l′ in the switching theorem.

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, Lemma3.6 with proof, pp.15–16 (published Lemma3.7)
sources.match: Proves that the residual monodromy on T′_0 and on T_0 is SL_n(k(λ)) under N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1, by the transvection argument, Zalesskii–Serezhkin and Lemma 3.1; the first assertion is stated for n > 2 only (PAPER-QIAN-23/E31).

nodes.title: Full symplectic residual monodromy of the self-dual family
nodes.statement: For the self-dual data (n even) and a nonzero prime λ of O^+ = ℤ[ζ_N, 1/(2N)]^+, the reduction of ρ_et on Ṽ_B/λ has image Sp(Ṽ_{B,t̃}/λ), and for every t ∈ T_0(ℂ) the map π_1(T_0(ℂ), t) → Sp(V_{B,t}/λ) is surjective. For n = 2 this gives SL_2(k(λ)) = Sp_2(k(λ)) on T_0(ℂ); the corresponding statement for Qian’s last-coordinate Y′ quotient is false for n=2; the BLGHT middle-coordinate quotient does have full Sp₂ monodromy (PAPER-QIAN-23/E31).
hypotheses: n even; λ a prime of the real cyclotomic ring, k(λ) its residue field (degree over 𝔽_l not necessarily the order of l mod N)
proofSteps: Absolute irreducibility as in DM.4/residual-monodromy-absolutely-irreducible; generation by elements with characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n and fixed space of dimension ≥ n − 1 as in DM.5/residual-monodromy-sl.

Zalesskii–Serezhkin (for n > 2) leaves SL_n(k), Sp_n(k), SU(n, k); the alternating pairing excludes SL_n and SU for n > 2 (a diagonal element of SU(n, k(λ)) not conjugate into Sp_n), and the field of traces is k(λ) because αB ≠ B for α ≠ ±1 (BLGHT11's argument).
On T_0(ℂ): the quotient by the index-N normal subgroup is cyclic of order dividing N, and the cyclic composition factors of Sp_n(𝔽_{l^r}) have order 2 or 3 (3 only for Sp_2(𝔽_3)), prime to N.
acceptance: n = 2: the residual monodromy of the real form mod λ is SL_2(k(λ)).

sources.match: The residual monodromy of the self-dual family is the full symplectic group, on T̃_0 and on T_0.

nodes.title: The skew-Hermitian Poincaré pairing on the residual Dwork local system
nodes.statement: Let n > 2, Qian's datum, and λ a place of M above l ∤ 2N with −1 ∈ ⟨l⟩ ⊂ (ℤ/Nℤ)^× (equivalently, the Frobenius of k(λ) over 𝔽_l contains complex conjugation c on μ_N). Then Poincaré duality on the relative cohomology with O_{M^+_λ}-coefficients, extended sesquilinearly to O_{M_λ}, and the Ψ-twist give a perfect 𝔽_l-bilinear pairing ⟨·,·⟩ : W̄_λ × W̄_λ → k(λ)(1 − n) with ⟨ax, y⟩ = a⟨x, y⟩, ⟨x, ay⟩ = c(a)⟨x, y⟩ and ⟨y, x⟩ = −c⟨x, y⟩, i.e. skew-Hermitian for k(λ)/k(λ)^c. Consequently the pairing places geometric monodromy in U_n(k(λ)); the trivial determinant supplied by DM.3/twisted-dwork-local-system further places it in SU_n(k(λ)) (after DM.0/hermitian-forms-unique), and every fibre W̄_{t,λ} is conjugate self-dual with multiplier ε̄^{1−n}.
hypotheses: −1 ∈ ⟨l⟩ mod N (the 'unitary case'); n > 2, N odd
proofSteps: DM.2/eigensheaf-duality pairs the χ-part with the χ^{−1}-part; c sends χ to χ^{−1}, and when c ∈ Gal(k(λ)/𝔽_l) the composition with the coefficient automorphism c gives a sesquilinear self-pairing of V̄_λ.

The middle cup product is alternating (N − 2 odd), which gives ⟨y, x⟩ = −c⟨x, y⟩; the twist by Ψ_λ^{−1} and the relation Ψ·c(Ψ) = ε^{n+1−N} (DM.3/twisting-hecke-character) shift the values from k(λ)(2 − N) to k(λ)(1 − n).

Choose η≠0 of trace zero and multiply the skew-Hermitian form by η. Its isometry group becomes the usual U_n after choosing an orthonormal basis. The determinant formula det W_λ=M_λ(n(1−n)/2) from DM.3 is geometrically trivial; this additional argument gives SU_n, independently of the later determinant-descends node.
acceptance: If l ≡ −1 mod N then k(λ) = 𝔽_{l²} and c is the Frobenius x ↦ x^l of 𝔽_{l²}.

sources.match: When −1 mod N lies in ⟨l_i⟩ there is a perfect pairing on W̄_{λ_i} with values in k(λ_i)(1 − n) satisfying the same two conditions, from Poincaré duality on the relative cohomology with O_{M^+_λ}-coefficients extended sesquilinearly.

nodes.title: Full special unitary residual monodromy in the unitary case
nodes.statement: Let n > 2, Qian's datum, l ∤ 2N with −1 ∈ ⟨l⟩ mod N and λ | l a place of M. Then the image of the geometric monodromy group π_1(T_{0,ℚ̄}) acting on W̄_λ is SU_n(k(λ)) for the skew-Hermitian structure of DM.5/hermitian-poincare-pairing.
hypotheses: n > 2, gcd(N, n) = 1
proofSteps: The image lies in SU_n(k(λ)) by DM.5/hermitian-poincare-pairing.

Run the argument of DM.5/residual-monodromy-sl: generation by transvections, Zalesskii–Serezhkin, exclusion of proper subfields and of Sp_n by DM.1/asymmetric-stabiliser-trivial; the remaining possibility is SU(n, k(λ)), now allowed.

The monodromy of T_0 is normal of index dividing N in that of T′_0; SU_n(k(λ)) is perfect with cyclic composition factors of order dividing n (DM.0/special-linear-unitary-simple), and gcd(N, n) = 1, so the image on T_0 is all of SU_n(k(λ)).
acceptance: For l ≡ −1 mod N and n = 3 the geometric monodromy of W̄_λ is SU_3(𝔽_{l²}).

sources.match: In the case −1 mod N ∈ ⟨l_i⟩ the proof of Qian's Lemma 3.7 gives a subgroup of SU_n of index dividing N, hence all of SU_n(k(λ_i)) since N is prime to n.

nodes.title: The determinant of the Dwork local systems is geometrically constant
nodes.statement: For every nonzero ideal 𝔫 of O (of O^+ for the self-dual data), the rank-one lisse sheaf ∧^n V[𝔫] on (T_0)_F, F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N), has trivial geometric monodromy, hence is the pullback of a character of G_F, determined by its stalk at t = 0. The same holds for ∧^n V_λ and for ∧^n W̄_λ (which is ε̄^{−n(n−1)/2}). This is descent of the determinant, not triviality of the arithmetic character.
hypotheses: T_0 geometrically connected over F
proofSteps: The geometric fundamental group of T′_0 is generated by γ_0, γ_1, γ_∞, whose images have determinant 1 (DM.4/monodromy-at-zero, DM.4/picard-lefschetz-at-one, DM.4/unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity); this persists after reduction and restriction to the finite-index subgroup of T_0.

A lisse sheaf on a geometrically connected F-variety with trivial geometric monodromy is the pullback of a G_F-representation (the homotopy exact sequence π_1^geom → π_1 → G_F); its value is read off at the F-point t = 0.
acceptance: For n = 3 and 𝔫 = λ, ∧³V[λ] is the character of G_F by which G_F acts on the top exterior power of the Fermat fibre.

sources.match: The monodromy of ∧^n V[𝔫] restricted to the geometric fundamental group is trivial because det(γ_0) = det(γ_1) = det(γ_∞) = 1, so it factors through G_F.

nodes.title: Moduli of level structures on Dwork local systems
nodes.statement: Let F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N) be a number field, l_1 ≠ l_2 primes not dividing 2N, λ_i places of M above l_i, and Λ = W̄_{λ_1} × W̄_{λ_2} (or V[𝔫] for 𝔫 = λ_1λ_2, or the self-dual V[𝔫]((N − 1 − n)/2) over O^+). Level-structure data are: (1) étale sheaves U_i on Spec F of free k(λ_i)-modules of rank n (i.e. continuous representations of G_F); (2) isomorphisms η_i : ∧^nW̄_{λ_i} ≅ ∧^nU_i over (T_0)_F (possible by DM.5/determinant-descends exactly when the determinant characters agree); (3) in the unitary case −1 ∈ ⟨l_i⟩, a perfect 𝔽_{l_i}-bilinear skew-Hermitian pairing U_i × U_i → k(λ_i)(1 − n), with η_i compatible with the pairings induced on ∧^n (in the self-dual case, a perfect alternating pairing with multiplier ε^{1−n} matching that of V[𝔫]). The functor T({U_i}) on (T_0)_F-schemes S, sending S to pairs of isomorphisms φ_i : W̄_{λ_i,S} ≅ U_{i,S} with ∧^nφ_i = η_i and preserving the pairings in the unitary (resp. symplectic) case, is represented by a finite étale (T_0)_F-scheme, a torsor under the finite étale group scheme SL(W̄_{λ_1}) × SL(W̄_{λ_2}) (resp. SU, Sp). This covers Qian's T_W (U_1 × U_2 = W, n > 2, split case), BLGHT11's T_W with the symplectic condition added in BLGGT14, and BCGNT25's T({U_{λ_i}}) (Definition 4.4.1, with places of M and the compatibility of η_i with the pairings, PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E22–E23). For one prime l ≡ 1 mod N write T(r̄_λ); for two primes ≡ ±1 mod N write T(r̄_{λ_1}, r̄_{λ_2}).
hypotheses: η_i compatible with the pairings in the unitary case (otherwise the functor can be empty)
the U_i are given as Galois representations of G_F
proofSteps: Étale locally both W̄ and U are constant and η is multiplication by a unit; the solutions form a coset of SL_n (resp. SU_n, Sp_n) inside GL_n, so the functor is an étale sheaf, locally constant with finite values.
Locally constant sheaves of finite sets on (T_0)_F are representable by finite étale covers (equivalently, finite π_1-sets); the group-scheme action is simply transitive.

Apply EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.0.2: the finite set of coefficient-linear isomorphisms is a continuous π₁-set, so it gives a finite étale cover. The pairing and determinant conditions cut out a π₁-stable subset. Its geometric fibres are the specified simply transitive classical-group sets when nonempty. R09.4 supplies the abstract torsor terminology; coherent O-module Isom schemes of R09.2 are not the construction used here.
acceptance: If U_i = W̄_{λ_i,t_0} for an F-point t_0, the identity is an F-point of T({U_i}) above t_0.

sources.match: Defines T_W(S) as the isomorphisms W_S ≅ V[𝔫]_S with top exterior power φ_S and asserts representability (it is in fact finite étale).

nodes.title: Residual monodromy at two primes is the full product
nodes.statement: Let l_1 ≠ l_2 be primes not dividing 2N with max(l_1, l_2) > 10, λ_i | l_i, and suppose each factor's geometric monodromy is the full group H_i ∈ {SL_n(k(λ_i)) (n > 2, −1 ∉ ⟨l_i⟩), SU_n(k(λ_i)) (n > 2, −1 ∈ ⟨l_i⟩), Sp_n(k(λ_i)) (self-dual data)}. Then for every t ∈ T_0(ℂ) the geometric monodromy π_1(T_0(ℂ), t) → H_1 × H_2 is surjective.
hypotheses: l₁≠l₂ odd, prime to N, max(l₁,l₂)>10. This allows the small factor Sp₂(𝔽₃), which must not be called perfect.
proofSteps: Each projection is surjective (DM.5/residual-monodromy-sl, DM.5/residual-monodromy-su, DM.5/residual-monodromy-sp).

Relabel so that l₁>10. H₁ is perfect and each nontrivial quotient has its nonabelian simple projective quotient as a composition factor. Artin’s comparison rules out that simple factor among those of H₂. If H₂=Sp₂(𝔽₃), it is solvable, with only cyclic factors of orders 2 and 3, so it cannot share a nontrivial quotient with H₁. In all other cases use its usual projective simple factor. Goursat’s lemma now gives the full product; perfectness of H₂ in the exceptional case is neither asserted nor needed.
acceptance: For Qian's switching (l, l′ with l′ ≡ 1 mod N, l′ > 2ln + 5 > 10) the hypotheses hold with H_2 = SL_n(𝔽_{l′}).

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, Proposition3.7 with proof, p.16 (published Proposition3.8)
sources.match: By Lemma 3.7, Goursat's lemma, the normal subgroups of SL_n and Artin's theorem, the monodromy surjects onto SL_n(k(𝔓_1)) × SL_n(k(𝔓_2)).
The symplectic analogue for square-free 𝔫 whose prime factors have distinct residue characteristics.
The product of SL_n and SU_n factors, by Lemma 5.2.3 and Goursat's lemma.

nodes.title: The level-structure torsors are geometrically irreducible
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy (and for one prime l ≡ 1 mod N), with level data as in DM.5/level-structure-torsor (pairings compatible with η_i in the unitary case; symplectic compatibility in the self-dual case), the scheme T({U_i}) is a smooth, geometrically irreducible F-variety. This is Qian's Proposition 3.8, BLGHT11 Proposition 4.2(1) with BLGGT14's correction, and BCGNT25 Proposition 4.4.2 with the compatibility proviso.
hypotheses: η_i compatible with the pairings in the unitary case (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E23)
two primes with max > 10, or one prime l ≡ 1 mod N
proofSteps: T({U_i}) is finite étale over the smooth geometrically connected (T_0)_F, hence smooth; it is geometrically connected iff π_1(T_{0,ℚ̄}) acts transitively on a geometric fibre.
A geometric fibre is a torsor under ∏H_i (the groups preserving determinant and pairing), and the geometric monodromy surjects onto ∏H_i (DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy), so it acts transitively.
A smooth connected variety over a field of characteristic 0 is irreducible.
acceptance: For one prime l ≡ 1 mod N with k(λ) = 𝔽_l, T(r̄_λ) is geometrically irreducible because the monodromy of W̄_λ is SL_n(𝔽_l) (BCGNT25 Remark 4.4.3).
