T_W is geometrically connected for square-free 𝔫 with distinct residue characteristics.
T({U_{λ_i}}) is a geometrically irreducible smooth F-scheme; T(r̄_λ) likewise for one prime l ≡ 1 mod N.

nodes.title: Frobenius on the Fermat eigenlines is a product of Gauss sums
nodes.statement: Let F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N), v a finite place of F of residue characteristic p ∤ Nl with residue field of q elements, ψ : 𝔽_q → ℚ̄_l^× a nontrivial additive character and t : μ_N(𝔽_q) ≅ μ_N(ℚ̄_l) the identification through the place. For a ∈ ℤ/Nℤ put g(v, a) = −∑_{x∈𝔽_q^×} t(x^{(1−q)/N})^a ψ(x) (so g(v, 0) = 1). Then for i ∈ B(a) the geometric Frobenius at v acts on the eigenline V_{λ,i} of the Fermat fibre by the scalar q^{−1}∏_{j=1}^N g(v, a_j + i), which is independent of ψ; for i ∉ B(a) the eigenspace is zero.
hypotheses: v ∤ Nl
geometric Frobenius on cohomology
proofSteps: The Fermat fibre has good reduction at v and the eigenspace decomposition commutes with Frobenius (DM.2/fermat-fibre-splitting).

Weil's computation of the zeta function of the Fermat hypersurface by Jacobi sums, written as products of Gauss sums (Deligne, Hodge cycles, §7, Proposition 7.10), gives the eigenvalue on each character line; ψ-independence follows because ∑_j(a_j + i) ≡ 0 mod N.
The Lefschetz trace formula over 𝔽_{q^m} for the elements of H identifies the eigenvalues.
acceptance: N = 3, the line with character (1, 1, 1) of the Fermat cubic: Frobenius acts by q^{−1}g(v, 1)³, which is a Jacobi sum of a cubic character up to sign, of complex absolute value √q.

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, proof of Lemma3.8, p.17 (published Lemma3.9)
sources.match: Frobenius acts on V_{λ,i} by q^{−1}∏_j g(v, a_j + i), with the Gauss sum defined through a fixed additive character, citing Deligne Proposition I.7.10.

sources.locator: Updated author chapter (1 October 2018), §7, Proposition7.10, pp.48–50
sources.match: Frobenius eigenvalues on the character lines of the cohomology of Fermat hypersurfaces are products of Gauss sums.

nodes.title: Gauss-sum formula for the determinant of the Dwork motive
nodes.statement: For v ∤ Nl of odd residue characteristic with q = #k(v): det(Frob_v | V_{λ,0}) = q^{−n}∏_{b∈B}∏_{j=1}^{N} g(v, a_j + b) = q^{n(N−n−2)/2}(∏_{b∈B} g(v, b))^n. Equivalently ∏_{b∈B}∏_j g(v, a_j + b) = (∏_{b∈B} g(v, b))^n q^{n(N−1)/2 − n(n−1)/2}. By DM.5/determinant-descends this computes the character det V[λ] of G_F at Frob_v.
hypotheses: residue characteristic of v odd and prime to Nl (so (q − 1)/N is even)
proofSteps: For Qian's data the residues a_j + b (j = 1, …, N) run over b itself n + 1 times (from the n + 1 zeros) and over every s ≠ −b′, b′ ∈ B, at most once; regroup the double product as (∏g(v, b))^n · (∏_{s≠0}g(v, s))^n / ∏_{i≠j} g(v, b_j − b_i).
Use g(v, a)g(v, −a) = (−1)^{a(q−1)/N}q = q for a ≠ 0 (q − 1 even, N odd; Mathlib gaussSum_mul_gaussSum_eq_card) to evaluate ∏_{s≠0} g(v, s) = q^{(N−1)/2} and ∏_{i≠j} g(v, b_j − b_i) = q^{n(n−1)/2}.
Combine with the factor q^{−n} of DM.6/fermat-frobenius-gauss-sums.
acceptance: Weight check: |g(v, b)| = √q, so |det| = q^{n(N−n−2)/2}·q^{n²/2} = q^{n(N−2)/2}, consistent with purity of weight N − 2 in rank n.

nodes.title: The Gauss-sum product descends to the cyclotomic coefficients
nodes.statement: For v ∤ Nl of residue characteristic p: ∏_{b∈B} g(v, b) ∈ ℚ_l(ζ_N). For the self-dual data with n = 2 (B = −B), g(v, b_1)g(v, b_2) ∈ ℚ_l(ζ_N)^+ = ℚ_l(ζ_N + ζ_N^{−1}).
hypotheses: ∑_{b∈B} b ≡ 0 mod N
for n = 2: B = −B
proofSteps: An automorphism σ of ℚ̄_l fixing ℚ_l(ζ_N) acts on p-th roots of unity by ζ_p ↦ ζ_p^a, a ∈ 𝔽_p^×; substituting x ↦ a^{−1}x gives σ(g(v, b)) = t(a^{(q−1)/N})^b g(v, b), and the product over B picks up t(a^{(q−1)/N})^{∑b} = 1.

For n = 2 let σ fix ℚ_l(ζ_N)^+; it acts on μ_N by ζ ↦ ζ^{±1} and on μ_p by some a; then σ(g(v, b)) = t(a^{(q−1)/N})^{±b}g(v, ±b), and the product over B = −B with b_1 + b_2 ≡ 0 is invariant. No σ fixing ζ_p need exist (the printed proof assumes one; PAPER-QIAN-23/E33).
acceptance: n = 2, l = 3, N = 301, p = 5: no σ ∈ G_{ℚ_3(ζ_N)^+} inverts ζ_N and fixes ζ_5, yet the argument above applies.

nodes.title: The determinant of the residual Dwork motive is an n-th power up to 𝔽_{l²}
nodes.statement: Let F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N) and λ a prime above l of O (of O^+ when n = 2), k(λ) its residue field. The character det V[λ] of G_F (DM.5/determinant-descends) takes values in (𝔽_{l²}^× k(λ)^×)^n ⊂ 𝔽̄_l^×; it takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n when 𝔽_{l²} ⊆ k(λ).
hypotheses: determinant read at t = 0
the factor q^{n(N−n−2)/2} is an n-th power after a quadratic coefficient extension when n is even
proofSteps: By Chebotarev it suffices to evaluate at Frobenius elements at v ∤ 2Nl; DM.6/dwork-determinant-gauss-formula gives q^{n(N−n−2)/2}(∏g(v, b))^n.
∏g(v, b) is λ-integral in ℚ_l(ζ_N) (resp. ℚ_l(ζ_N)^+) by DM.6/gauss-product-descent, so its reduction lies in k(λ).
q^{n(N−n−2)/2} = (q^{(N−n−2)/2})^n when N − n is even, and otherwise (√q)^{n(N−n−2)} with √q in 𝔽_{l²}.
acceptance: If l ≡ 1 mod N and n odd, the character takes values in (𝔽_l^×)^n.

sources.match: The determinant of V[λ] as a G_F-representation lands in (𝔽_{l²}^× k(λ)^×)^n.

nodes.title: Matching determinants at the coefficient prime l
nodes.statement: Let n = l^a m with l ∤ m, F a CM field, M = F(ζ_N), r̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l^s}) continuous, and λ | l a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2) whose residue field k(λ) contains 𝔽_{l²} and all m-th roots of all elements of 𝔽_{l^s}. Then (i) det r̄ takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n; (ii) det V[λ] (a character of G_M) takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n; (iii) the character det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄|_{G_M})^{−1} takes values in (k(λ)^×)^n; (iv) μ_m(𝔽̄_l) ⊂ k(λ), so m | #k(λ)^× and the n-th power map on k(λ)^× has kernel μ_m. Thus the finite-coefficient root problem has exponent m; applying Qian Lemma 2.1 requires the finite-coefficient strengthening requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 (the paper requires n | #k(λ)^× instead, which fails when l | n; PAPER-QIAN-23/E5).
hypotheses: k(λ) ⊇ 𝔽_{l²} and all m-th roots of elements of 𝔽_{l^s}
proofSteps: For x ∈ 𝔽_{l^s}^× pick y ∈ k(λ) with y^m = x; the l^a-th power map is bijective on k(λ)^×, so y = z^{l^a} and x = z^n.
DM.6/determinant-nth-power with 𝔽_{l²} ⊆ k(λ) gives (ii); (iii) follows; (iv) applies the hypothesis to x = 1.

The l^a-power automorphism of k× makes the n-th-root and m-th-root problems equivalent. The requested supplier result must produce a root valued in k× after a totally real base change, with the avoidance condition and simultaneous roots needed in DM.9. A root in Q̄_l× alone does not imply a root in this fixed finite field.
acceptance: n = l = 3, s = 1: m = 1, so every character into (k(λ)^×)^3 = k(λ)^× already has a cube root, and the condition n | #k(λ)^× of the published text would wrongly fail.

sources.match: Applies Lemma 3.9 over F(ζ_N) to see that det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄)^∨ has image in (k(λ)^×)^n, under conditions on N giving 𝔽_{l²} and the m-th roots inside k(λ).
n-th roots of (𝔽_{l^r}^×)^n-valued characters after a totally real base change avoiding a given field; the atlas plans it in ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4.

nodes.title: Matching determinants at the auxiliary prime l′ ≡ 1 mod N
nodes.statement: Let l′ be an odd prime with l′ ≡ 1 mod N and λ′ | l′ a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2), so k(λ′) = 𝔽_{l′} and ℚ(ζ_N)_{λ′} = ℚ_{l′}. For v ∤ 2Nl′ with q = #k(v) and geometric Frobenius Frob_v: (i) det(Frob_v | V_{λ′,0})·q^{−n(n−1)/2} = (q^{(N−2n−1)/2}∏_{b∈B} g(v, b))^n, with q^{(N−2n−1)/2}∏g(v, b) ∈ ℤ_{l′}^×; equivalently det V_{λ′} ⊗ ε_{l′}^{n(n−1)/2} takes the value (q^{(N−2n−1)/2}∏g(v, b))^n at Frob_v. (ii) Hence for every continuous r̄′ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l′}) with det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}, the character (det r̄′|_{G_M})^{−1} ⊗ det V[λ′] takes values in (𝔽_{l′}^×)^n. (iii) If moreover l′ ≡ 1 mod n, then μ_n ⊂ 𝔽_{l′} and the finite-coefficient root theorem requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 applies with exponent n. The printed argument uses the statement of Lemma 3.9 (values only in (𝔽_{l′²}^×)^n) and the sign det r̄′ = ε̄^{+n(n−1)/2}; the cancellation in (i), the sign and the sufficient congruence l′ ≡ 1 mod n are the corrections PAPER-QIAN-23/E6, E9, E7.
hypotheses: l′ ≡ 1 mod N (and mod n for (iii))
ε_{l′}^{−1}(Frob_v) = q for geometric Frobenius
proofSteps: (i) is a rearrangement of DM.6/dwork-determinant-gauss-formula: q^{n(N−n−2)/2}·q^{−n(n−1)/2} = (q^{(N−2n−1)/2})^n, with N odd making the exponent an integer; the base is an l′-adic unit because |g(v, b)|_{l′} = 1 for v ∤ l′.
ε_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2}(Frob_v) = q^{n(n−1)/2}, so (det r̄′)^{−1} cancels the remaining power of q; the reduction of the base lies in 𝔽_{l′}.
μ_n ⊂ 𝔽_{l′} when l′ ≡ 1 mod n; such primes with l′ ≡ 1 mod Nn have positive density.

The congruence modulo n is a sufficient way to meet Qian Lemma 2.1, not a necessary condition for existence of a root. If gcd(n,l′−1)=1, powering is an automorphism and every finite-field-valued character already has a unique n-th root. In general one can instead use d=gcd(n,l′−1) in the finite-field root obstruction.
acceptance: For r̄′ = Sym^{n−1} r̄_{E_0,l′} with r̄_{E_0,l′} = H¹_ét(E_0, 𝔽_{l′}) (determinant ε̄^{−1}) the hypothesis det r̄′ = ε̄^{−n(n−1)/2} holds.

nodes.title: Frobenius polynomials of Dwork fibres are integral and independent of λ
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ(ζ_N) be a number field, v a finite place of F of residue characteristic l′ ∤ N, and t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}). For every place λ of M of residue characteristic ≠ l′, W_{t,λ} (and V_{t,λ}) is unramified at v, and Q_v(X) = det(X − Frob_v | W_{t,λ}) has coefficients in M, integral at every λ whose residue characteristic differs from l′, and is independent of λ. Full O_M-integrality is concluded after the crystalline argument in DM.7.
hypotheses: t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}), i.e. t integral with t^N − 1 a unit (good reduction)
proofSteps: Y_t is smooth and proper over O_{F_v}; smooth proper base change makes H^{N−2}_ét(Y_{t,F̄_v}, O_{M_λ}) unramified and identifies it with the cohomology of the special fibre.

For each h∈H₀, apply Katz–Messing Theorem 2(1)–(2), pp. 76–77, to the algebraic correspondence given by h composed with a Frobenius power and the rational Künneth projector. Its traces on the required cohomological degree are rational and independent of the cohomology theory. Taking the finite character-weighted sum of these traces gives M-valued traces on e_χ, hence characteristic polynomials by Newton identities. The Hecke-character twist is compatible in λ by DM.3/twisting-hecke-character. RD.7 is requested to include this equivariant form, not just the untwisted total polynomial.

The finite free O_{M_λ}-lattices give integrality at all λ∤l′. This node does not yet give integrality at λ|l′. After crystalline comparison, DM.7 uses the nonnegative filtration jumps of W and weak admissibility to supply that last input; no prerequisite from DM.6 back to DM.7 is used here.
acceptance: deg Q_v = n and the roots of Q_v have complex absolute value q_v^{(n−1)/2} (purity of weight n − 1).

sources.locator: arXiv:2309.15880v3, Proposition4.2.5(1) with proof, pp.42–43; integrality completed only in DM.7 (E27)
sources.match: W_{t,λ} is unramified at v and Q_v has coefficients in O_M independent of λ, by smooth proper base change and Katz–Messing Theorem 2(2).

nodes.title: Twisted de Rham eigenspaces of the Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let H_dR = H^{N−2}_dR(Y/(T_0 × ℚ(ζ_N))), locally free with Hodge filtration F^j by local direct summands. For σ ∈ Gal(ℚ(ζ_N)/ℚ) put H_{dR,σ} = H_dR ⊗_{σ^{−1}, ℚ(ζ_N)} ℚ(ζ_N) (the right factor viewed as coefficients) and V_{dR,σ} = e_χ H_{dR,σ}, the χ-eigensheaf for H_0 acting through the coefficients, with filtration F^jV_{dR,σ} and graded pieces gr^j. At t = 0, V_{dR,σ,0} = ⊕_{i} V_{dR,σ,i} under the characters χ_i of H. For K/ℚ_l finite containing the base image of ℚ(ζ_N), V=V_{λ,t}⊗_{O_λ}E is an E-linear representation of G_K. Form D_dR,K(V)=(B_dR⊗_{ℚ_l}V)^{G_K}, a filtered module over K⊗_{ℚ_l}E. After extending E to a finite E′ containing every embedding of K, its σ-labelled component is D_dR,K(V)⊗_{K⊗E,σ⊗ι}E′. Equivariant de Rham comparison identifies it with the corresponding coefficient-conjugate χ-part of H^{N−2}_dR(Y_t/K)⊗_{K,σ}E′; the character is obtained by transporting χ along the same coefficient embedding ι. Expressed over the fixed global coefficient field, this is the σ^{−1}χ convention of the first part. No K-action on V is assumed.
hypotheses: characteristic 0 base T_0 × ℚ(ζ_N)
λ and v of the same residue characteristic l

Numerical weights in this roadmap are cohomological: a weight h means dim gr^h D_dR,σ, so HT(ε_l)=−1. PadicHodgeTheory uses HT(ε_l)=+1 and gr^{−h}; negate its labelled weights when importing it. PL.0 uses the cohomological convention already.
proofSteps: Relative Hodge bundles of a smooth proper family in characteristic 0 are locally free, the Hodge spectral sequence degenerates and character idempotents cut out locally free summands with the induced filtration (ComplexComparisonPartII C5).
The filtered de Rham comparison for proper smooth varieties over p-adic fields (CohomologyComparisons CP.3) is H_0-equivariant; taking χ-parts introduces the twist by σ.
acceptance: For σ = id and t = 0, V_{dR,id,0} = ⊕_{i∈B} V_{dR,i} with one-dimensional summands.

nodes.title: Hodge grades of the Fermat eigenlines
nodes.statement: Write σ^{−1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^a and ⟨x⟩ for the representative of x mod N in {1, …, N}. Then V_{dR,σ,i} ≠ 0 iff i ∈ B, it is then one-dimensional, and its only nonzero graded piece is in degree M(a) + #{b ∈ B : ⟨ab⟩ < ⟨ai⟩}, where M(a) = (∑_j⟨a·a_j + 1⟩)/N − 1; equivalently the degree is (∑_j⟨a(a_j + i)⟩)/N − 1. For the self-dual data (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.2(1)) the degree is (N − n − 3)/2 + #{b ∈ B : ⟨ab⟩ ≤ ⟨ai⟩}.
hypotheses: a ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^× determined by σ
Use a zero-shaped exponent datum: zero has multiplicity n+1, each nonzero residue occurs at most once, and 0∉B. Rank n alone does not imply this consecutive-grade computation.
proofSteps: After base change along τ_0σ^{−1} to ℂ, gr^jV_{dR,σ,i} is the eigenspace of H^{j, N−2−j}(Y_0(ℂ)) for the character (a(a_j + i))_j of H.
DM.2/fermat-hypersurface-cohomology: nonzero iff all a(a_j + i) ≢ 0 (i.e. i ∈ B), in Hodge degree j with j + 1 = ∑⟨a(a_j + i)⟩/N.
Set j(d) = ∑⟨a·a_j + d⟩/N − 1; it increases by one when passing d ≡ ab, b ∈ B, and is constant otherwise; induct from M(a) = j(1).
acceptance: For σ = id (a = 1) and Qian's datum with n = 3, the three lines i = 1, 2, N − 3 have consecutive grades M(1), M(1) + 1, M(1) + 2.

nodes.title: Consecutive Hodge numbers of the Dwork motives
nodes.statement: For each σ, gr^jV_{dR,σ} is locally free of rank one on T_0 × ℚ(ζ_N) for M(a) ≤ j ≤ M(a) + n − 1 and zero otherwise; V_{dR,σ} is locally free of rank n. For the self-dual data the range is (N − 1 − n)/2 ≤ j ≤ (N + n − 3)/2 (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.2(2)).
hypotheses: Hodge numbers are locally constant in a smooth proper family in characteristic 0
Use a zero-shaped exponent datum: zero has multiplicity n+1, each nonzero residue occurs at most once, and 0∉B. Rank n alone does not imply this consecutive-grade computation.
proofSteps: gr^jV_{dR,σ} is locally free (DM.7/twisted-de-rham-eigenspaces), so its rank can be computed at t = 0.
At t = 0 the grades of the n eigenlines are M(a) + #{b : ⟨ab⟩ < ⟨ai⟩}, which run through M(a), …, M(a) + n − 1 as i runs through B ordered by ⟨ai⟩ (DM.7/hodge-grades-of-fermat-eigenlines).

nodes.title: Dwork fibres are de Rham with consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights
nodes.statement: Let v | l be a place of F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N) and t ∈ T_0(F_v). (1) V_{λ,t} ⊗ ℚ(ζ_N)_λ is a de Rham representation of G_{F_v} (not of G_F; PAPER-QIAN-23/E8), and for an embedding σ : F_v ↪ ℚ̄_l with σ^{−1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^a on ℚ(ζ_N), its σ-labelled Hodge–Tate weights (cohomological convention) are M(a), M(a) + 1, …, M(a) + n − 1, each with multiplicity one. (2) W_{t,λ} is de Rham with HT_σ(W_{t,λ}) = {0, 1, …, n − 1} for every σ. (3) For the self-dual data V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2) is de Rham with Hodge–Tate numbers {0, …, n − 1} at every embedding (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(1)).
hypotheses: l the residue characteristic of λ and v

Cohomological weights are the positive filtration jumps, opposite to PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/hodge-tate-weight-convention. Thus W has supplier weights {0,−1,…,1−n}, while PL.0 assigns it ordinary weight 0.
proofSteps: (1) is DM.7/twisted-de-rham-eigenspaces with DM.7/consecutive-hodge-numbers.
(2): W_{t,λ} = V_{t,λ} ⊗ Ψ_λ^{−1} has weights shifted by a constant M′_σ; det W_λ ≅ M_λ(n(1 − n)/2) (DM.3/twisted-dwork-local-system) gives nM′_σ + n(n − 1)/2 = n(n − 1)/2, so M′_σ = 0.
(3) as in (1) with the Tate twist.
acceptance: For n = 3 and every embedding, the weights of W_{t,λ} are {0, 1, 2}.

W_{t,λ} is de Rham with HT_τ = {0, …, n − 1}, by Qian's lemma and the determinant.
Hodge–Tate numbers {0, …, n − 1} of V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2).

nodes.title: Crystallinity and Frobenius at good-reduction fibres
nodes.statement: Let v | l, l ∤ N, and t ∈ O_{F_v} with t^N − 1 a unit. Then V_{λ,t} and W_{t,λ} are crystalline representations of G_{F_v}; the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v on WD(W_{t,λ}) equals Q_v(X) of the special fibre (the same polynomial as for λ′ ∤ l, DM.6/frobenius-polynomials-independent); and W_{t,λ} is ordinary iff the roots of Q_v in ℚ̄_l have l-adic valuations 0, f, 2f, …, (n − 1)f, f = [k(v) : 𝔽_l]. No crystallinity is claimed at the punctures or for t merely integral. For the self-dual data, V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2) is crystalline under the same condition (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(2)). Moreover Q_v(X) for W has coefficients integral at λ|l as well, so the M-valued polynomial of DM.6 belongs to O_M[X].
hypotheses: l ∤ N

Use φ^f on a K₀ coefficient component, v_l(l)=1 and f=[k(v):𝔽_l]; translate supplier Hodge–Tate signs by using its filtration jumps. The equivariant comparison and the rank-one crystalline Hecke twist are both required.
proofSteps: Y_t has good reduction over O_{F_v}; the crystalline comparison theorem gives crystallinity of H^{N−2}_ét and an H_0- and Frobenius-equivariant identification of D_cris with crystalline cohomology of the special fibre; Ψ_λ is crystalline at v.
The characteristic polynomial of φ^f on the twisted χ-part of crystalline cohomology equals Q_v by Katz–Messing (applicable to crystalline cohomology by Gillet–Messing).
Regular consecutive weights {0, …, n − 1} and the slope criterion for ordinarity (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2) give the last statement.

At λ|l all filtration jumps of W are 0,…,n−1. Weak admissibility applied to the lowest-slope Frobenius subobject shows its Newton degree is nonnegative, since its induced Hodge degree is nonnegative. Hence every Frobenius slope is ≥0, and the polynomial is λ-integral. Together with DM.6 integrality away from l this proves O_M-integrality, without assuming it earlier.
acceptance: If the special fibre point x has Q_x with l-adic slopes 0, 1, …, n − 1 (normalised), W_{t,λ} is crystalline ordinary.

sources.match: For t ∈ O_{F_v} with t^N − 1 ∉ 𝔪, V_{λ,t} is crystalline because Y_t has good reduction.
Crystallinity, the Frobenius characteristic polynomial Q_v via Katz–Messing and Gillet–Messing, and the slope criterion for ordinarity (Geraghty Lemma 2.32).

nodes.statement: Let l ≡ 1 mod N (so ℚ(ζ_N)_λ = ℚ_l), v | l and t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}. Then V_{λ,t} is ordinary of weight μ with μ_{σ,i} = M(a_σ) for all i (in the convention of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0, cohomological weights M(a_σ), …, M(a_σ) + n − 1), where σ^{−1}(ζ_N) = ζ_N^{a_σ}. For the self-dual data, V_{λ,t}((N − 1 − n)/2) is ordinary of weight 0, and its reduction at t = 0 is 𝔽_l ⊕ 𝔽_l(−1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔽_l(1 − n) as a module for inertia (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.3(3)–(4)).
hypotheses: l ≡ 1 mod N
t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}
proofSteps: For t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}, Y_t and Y_0 have the same special fibre, so D_cris(V_{λ,t}) ≅ D_cris(V_{λ,0}) as φ-modules (crystalline comparison); their labelled Hodge–Tate weights agree (DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights).
By the slope criterion (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2, the crystalline form of BLGHT Lemma 2.2), V_{λ,t} is ordinary iff V_{λ,0} is.

V_{λ,0} ⊗ ℚ̄_l = ⊕_{i∈B} V_{λ,i}, each a crystalline character of G_{ℚ_l(ζ_N)_v} = G_{ℚ_l} with Hodge–Tate weight M(a_σ) + #{b : ⟨a_σb⟩ < ⟨a_σi⟩}, so as an inertia module it is ⊕_{i=0}^{n−1} ℚ̄_l(−M(a_σ) − i): an ordinary filtration.
acceptance: For the self-dual data and l ≡ 1 mod N the inertia action on the Fermat fibre mod λ is 𝔽_l ⊕ 𝔽_l(−1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝔽_l(1 − n) (after the Tate twist).

sources.match: For l ≡ 1 mod N and t ∈ 𝔪_{F_v}, V_{λ,t} is ordinary of weight (M(a_σ)), by comparison with the Fermat fibre.
The self-dual analogue, ordinary of weight 0, and the inertia action on the Fermat fibre mod λ.

nodes.title: Inertia on the Fermat fibre when l ≡ −1 mod N
nodes.statement: Let n>2, l>n prime with l≡−1 mod N, v|l of ℚ(ζ_N), λ|l of M, and τ,cτ:k(v)→k(λ)=𝔽_{l²}. Normalize Art to send a uniformizer to geometric Frobenius, set ω_τ=τ∘Art⁻¹ on inertia, and put θ_τ=ω_τ⁻¹. Then θ_τθ_{cτ}=ε̄_l⁻¹ and W̄_{0,λ}|I ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n θ_τ^{i−1}θ_{cτ}^{n−i}. This is BCGNT Lemma 4.4.4 with the inverse characters required by its determinant and cohomological conventions (E31). For the separately defined self-dual n=2 system use BLGHT Lemma 5.3(5) with the same sign translation; this statement does not invoke an undefined rank-two W.
hypotheses: n>2, l≡−1 mod N and l>n; the zero-shaped data and the W construction of DM.3.
ω and θ are inertia characters; θ is the reduction of the positive cohomological Lubin–Tate character, θ(Art(u))=τ(u)⁻¹ for units u.
proofSteps: H extends the H_0-action on the Fermat fibre and decomposes W̄_{0,λ} into n lines W̄_{0,λ,j}, the Ψ^{−1}-twists of the H-eigenspaces in H^{N−2} (printed H^{N−1}, PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E9), each crystalline of rank one.
The skew-Hermitian pairing (DM.5/hermitian-poincare-pairing) is orthogonal for this decomposition, so W̄_{0,λ,j}^c ≅ W̄_{0,λ,j}^∨ε̄^{1−n}.

Order the crystalline Fermat eigenlines by their τ-labelled filtration jumps i−1. The paired conjugate jump is n−i. Rank-one Fontaine–Laffaille in the range 0,…,n−1 gives θ_τ^{i−1}θ_{cτ}^{n−i}; using ω instead would give the dual signs. Their determinant is (θ_τθ_{cτ})^{n(n−1)/2}=ε̄_l^{−n(n−1)/2}, agreeing with DM.3.
acceptance: For n=3 the inertia summands are θ_{cτ}², θ_τθ_{cτ}, θ_τ²; their determinant is ε̄_l⁻³. With the printed positive ω powers it would instead be ε̄_l³. For l>7 these differ.
The analogous cohomological H¹ of a supersingular elliptic curve has inertia ω₂⁻¹⊕ω₂^{−l}; this is the separately defined rank-two boundary, not a W construction.

sources.locator: arXiv:2309.15880v3, Lemma4.4.4 with proof, p.48; invert the printed Artin fundamental characters (E31)
sources.match: The Fermat decomposition and paired labelled weights give this inertia formula after inverting the printed fundamental characters; §1.6 fixes Art and the cyclotomic sign. The determinant test in E31 detects the printed inconsistency.
The self-dual analogue for l ≡ −1 mod N.

sources.locator: §1.4, Lemma 1.4.1 and following product formula, pp. 5–6
sources.match: With Art taking a uniformizer to geometric Frobenius, the direct fundamental characters multiply to the cyclotomic character; the positive cohomological characters used here are their inverses.

nodes.title: Maximal unipotent local monodromy at places with v(t) < 0
nodes.statement: Let v be a finite place of F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N) and λ′ a prime of residue characteristic l′ ≠ char(v), l′ odd and prime to N, and residue characteristic of v prime to N. (1) If t ∈ O_{F_v} and t^N − 1 is a unit, V_{λ′,t} is unramified at v. (2) If v(t) < 0, V_{λ′,t}|_{G_{F_v}} is tamely ramified, inertia acts unipotently through exp(t_{l′}(σ)N) and the monodromy operator N of its Weil–Deligne representation has minimal polynomial X^n (a single Jordan block); for the self-dual data a Frobenius lift has characteristic polynomial (X − α)(X − αq)⋯(X − αq^{n−1}) with α = ±1 (after the twist (N − 1 − n)/2), i.e. WD is an unramified twist of Steinberg (BLGHT11 Lemma 5.1). The hypothesis v(t) < 0 is necessary (PAPER-QIAN-23/E1).
hypotheses: l′ ≠ residue characteristic of v
residue characteristic of v does not divide N; smooth proper base change and tame specialization are asserted over this good base only.
proofSteps: (1) is smooth proper base change.

(2): near t = ∞ the family over the punctured disc {v(t) < 0} has geometric monodromy generated by the local monodromy at ∞, which is a single unipotent Jordan block over ℚ̄_{l′} (DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity, applied to every conjugate character).

The Galois action of G_{F_v} on the fibre at t factors through the local fundamental group of the punctured disc at ∞ (tame specialisation of nearby cycles); inertia maps to the d-th power of the local monodromy generator, d = −v(t) > 0, still a single unipotent block in characteristic 0 (the argument of HSBT10 Lemma 1.15(2)).
For the Frobenius eigenvalues, the weight filtration of a single Jordan block and purity of the special value at ∞ give the Steinberg shape (BLGHT11).
acceptance: For the self-dual data with n = 2 and v(t) < 0, V_{λ′,t} is an unramified twist of the Steinberg representation at v, as for an elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction.

sources.locator: Published Lemma3.12, pp.1267–1268, was not present in v1 or independently read. The supported formulation here uses BLGHT Lemma5.1 and the explicit tame-specialization gap; E2 remains unverified as a publication-specific allegation
sources.match: Unverified publication cross-reference only. The roadmap’s v(t)<0 statement is checked using BLGHT Lemma5.1; tame specialization remains an explicit supplier gap.
Unramified for integral t with t^N − 1 a unit; tamely ramified with a single unipotent Jordan block and Steinberg-shaped Frobenius for t ∉ O_F.

nodes.title: The Dwork fibres form weakly compatible systems
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ(ζ_N) be a number field, t ∈ T_0(F) and S the finite places v with v | N or t ∉ T_0(O_{F_v}). Then (M, S, {Q_v(X)}_{v∉S}, {W^{ss}_{t,λ}}_λ, {{0, 1, …, n − 1}}_τ) is a weakly compatible system of l-adic representations of G_F over M of rank n, pure of weight n − 1 (BLGGT14 §5.1); the untwisted system {V_{t,λ}} instead has purity weight N−2 and Hodge–Tate multisets {M(a_τ), …, M(a_τ) + n − 1} and for the self-dual data over M^+ (with symplectic pairings).
proofSteps: Away from S and the residue characteristic of λ, W_{t,λ} is unramified with Frobenius polynomial Q_v independent of λ (DM.6/frobenius-polynomials-independent).

At v | l with v ∉ S, W_{t,λ} is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, n − 1} and the same Frobenius polynomial (DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction, DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights); at every v | l it is de Rham. The final clause of DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction now supplies O_M-integrality of Q_v; it was not an input to DM.6.
Purity of weight n − 1 is Deligne's theorem for the smooth fibres twisted by Ψ of weight N − n − 1.
acceptance: deg Q_v = n, Q_v(0) = ± q_v^{n(n−1)/2}, as the determinant ε^{−n(n−1)/2} requires.

sources.match: The family (M, S, {Q_v}, {W^{ss}_{t,λ}}, {{0, …, n − 1}}) is a weakly compatible system of rank n, pure of weight n − 1, in the sense of BLGGT14 §5.1.
Definition of weakly compatible systems of l-adic representations.

nodes.title: Generic slopes of indecomposable lisse sheaves (Drinfeld–Kedlaya)
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth irreducible variety over a finite field of characteristic p and E a lisse ℚ̄_{l′}-sheaf of rank n on X (l′ ≠ p) which is algebraic (Frobenius characteristic polynomials with algebraic coefficients). Fix a p-adic valuation on ℚ̄ and for x ∈ |X| let a^x_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ a^x_n be the p-adic slopes of Frob_x normalised by deg x. (i) There are rational numbers a^η_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ a^η_n such that the set U of x with a^x_i = a^η_i for all i is nonempty and has open intersection with the closed points of every curve (the intersection may be empty); (ii) ∑_{i≤r} a^x_i ≤ ∑_{i≤r} a^η_i for all x, r; (iii) if E is indecomposable then a^η_i − a^η_{i+1} ≤ 1 for 1 ≤ i < n.
hypotheses: E algebraic; (iii) requires E indecomposable (e.g. geometrically irreducible)
proofSteps: For a smooth curve, Drinfeld–Kedlaya §5.1 uses Abe’s crystalline companions for irreducible sheaves and Theorem 1.1.5 for convergent F-isocrystals; §5.2 handles indecomposable extensions. For higher-dimensional X, §5.3 restricts to suitable curves. This does not assume a global crystalline companion on an arbitrary variety. The companions and full-faithfulness inputs remain recorded supplier gaps.
(ii) is Grothendieck's specialisation theorem for Newton polygons.
acceptance: For E pure of weight n − 1 with slopes 0, 1, …, n − 1 at one point, (ii) and (iii) force the generic slopes to be 0, 1, …, n − 1.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.3.3, pp. 4–5 (arXiv v11); proof in §5, pp. 11–12
sources.match: For an algebraic lisse sheaf on a smooth variety over a finite field, generic slopes exist and are attained on a dense set, special slopes lie above generic ones, and for indecomposable sheaves consecutive generic slopes differ by at most one.
Applies DK17 Theorem 1.3.3 to the lisse sheaf W_μ with λ-adic slopes.

nodes.title: Generic crystalline ordinarity of the Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let v be a place of ℚ(ζ_N) of residue characteristic l ∤ N and λ a place of M of the same characteristic. There is a nonempty Zariski open U(v; λ) ⊂ T_{0,k(v)} such that for every finite extension F_w/ℚ(ζ_N)_v and every t ∈ T_0(O_{F_w}) whose reduction lies in U(v; λ)(k(w)), W_{t,λ} is a crystalline ordinary representation of G_{F_w}.
hypotheses: l ∤ N
Qian's datum, n > 2 (BCGNT25 setting)
proofSteps: By DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction it suffices that the normalised l-adic slopes s_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_n of Q_x (computed with an auxiliary μ of residue characteristic ≠ l) be n − 1, …, 1, 0 for x ∈ U.

W_μ is geometrically irreducible (DM.3/twisted-dwork-local-system); Drinfeld–Kedlaya (DM.7/drinfeld-kedlaya-slope-bound) give a dense open V with constant slopes and gaps ≤ 1; with ∑s_i = n(n − 1)/2 (determinant) it suffices to find U ⊂ V with s_n(x) = 0.

By (4.2.3) and the trace formula of E_μ (DM.3/hypergeometric-sheaf-properties), s_n(x) = 0 when tr(Frob_x | E_{μ,x}) ≢ 0 mod λ. Writing ρ_i through z ↦ z^{c_i}, the trace is congruent to N_{k/k(v)}(u(x)) for the polynomial u(T) = ∑_r(−1)^{nr}∏_i C(c_i, r)T^r (Lucas's theorem; one exponent in the printed proof is misprinted, PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E8); take U = T_{1,k(v)}[1/u] pulled back, nonempty since u(0) = 1.
acceptance: The open set is independent of the extension k/k(v): u has coefficients in k(v).

sources.match: Proves generic crystalline ordinarity by Drinfeld–Kedlaya, the determinant and a computation of the hypergeometric trace modulo λ following DK17 §A.3.

nodes.title: The equivariant semistable blowup of the reciprocal Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p ∤ N, W = W(k), and Spec W[T, U^{±1}]′ the open where (TU)^N ≠ 1. Let Y_N ⊂ ℙ^{N−1} × Spec W[T, U^{±1}]′ be UT(X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N) = N X_1⋯X_N (the Dwork family in the reciprocal parameter s = 1/t = UT), with D_i = {X_i = 0} and D = {∑X_i^N = 0}. Blow up D ∩ D_N, then successively the intersections of the strict transforms of D and D_j for j = N − 1, …, 1. The result 𝕏 satisfies: (a) every centre is H_0-stable, so H_0 acts on 𝕏 and the blowdown 𝕏 → Y_N is H_0-equivariant; (b) the blowdown is an isomorphism over T ≠ 0; (c) étale locally 𝕏 is étale over W[T, U^{±1}]′[Z_1, …, Z_r, Z_{r+1}^{±1}, …, Z_m^{±1}]/(TU − Z_1⋯Z_r), H_0-equivariantly with H_0 acting on the Z_i by characters. Base change along T ↦ π, U ↦ u (u ∈ O_F^×) gives a semistable model with H_0-action of uπ(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over O_F; base change to ℂ along U ↦ 1 gives a blowup of T(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over 𝔸¹ − μ_N, an isomorphism away from T = 0, whose fibre over 0 is a reduced normal crossings divisor without self-crossings.
hypotheses: p ∤ N
semistable: reduced normal crossings special fibre without self-intersections
proofSteps: The successive blowup centres are intersections of H_0-stable divisors, hence H_0-stable; blowups commute with flat base change.
Compute charts after each blowup by hand (QIAN21 pp. 5–8): the local equation becomes TU = Z_1⋯Z_r times a unit.
Remark 2.2 of QIAN21 records the H_0-equivariant charts.
acceptance: For N = 3 the fibre of Y_N over T = 0 is the triangle X_1X_2X_3 = 0 (three lines), already a reduced normal crossings divisor; the blowups resolve the singular points of the total space where D meets the coordinate lines.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2 and the paragraph after it, pp. 4–8 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: Constructs the H_0-equivariant blowup of UT(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i with semistable étale-local charts.
Uses the base change of this blowup to ℂ, whose fibre over 0 is a reduced normal crossings divisor.

nodes.title: Equivariant semistable models of Dwork fibres near infinity
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite containing ζ_N, p ∤ N, π a uniformiser, and t ∈ F with v(t) = d > 0 (the fibre at s = t, i.e. Dwork parameter t^{−1}). Then there are e ≥ 1 and a strictly semistable model 𝒴 over O_{F′}, F′ = F(π^{1/e}) totally ramified of degree e, of the hypersurface t(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i, with an H_0-action compatible with that on the generic fibre; 𝒴 is projective. More precisely there is an H_0-equivariant projective blowup Z of US^{de}(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over W[S, U^{±1}]′, an isomorphism outside S = 0, étale locally étale over W[U^{±1}, S, Z_1, …, Z_m]/(US − Z_1⋯Z_r) with some Z_i inverted, and 𝒴 is its base change along S ↦ π^{1/e}, U ↦ u. Only semistability over F′ (not over F) is asserted.
hypotheses: p ∤ N
v(t) > 0 (reciprocal parameter), i.e. the Dwork parameter has negative valuation
proofSteps: Base change the model of DM.8/dwork-semistable-blowup along T ↦ S^{de}; it becomes toroidal (log smooth) but not semistable.

Subdivide the slice S = 1 of its conical complex into unimodular lattice simplices (equivariant toroidal semistable reduction, Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat, owned by SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4); the corresponding blowup is H_0-equivariant and semistable after the ramified base change of degree e.
A blowup of a projective scheme is projective.
acceptance: d = 1 needs no subdivision: the model of DM.8/dwork-semistable-blowup is already semistable over O_F (e = 1).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 1.5, p. 3; restated as Theorem 2.3, p. 9; proof pp. 8–13 (arXiv v1)

nodes.title: The log special fibre of the semistable model lifts over W[T]
nodes.statement: In the setting of DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model, give Z the log structure M of the divisor (S) and 𝒴 that of (π^{1/e}). Choose u′ ∈ W^× with the same reduction as u and let (Y, N) be the base change of (Z, M) along S ↦ T, U ↦ u′ over Spec W[T]′ ((T^{de}u′)^N ≠ 1). Then (a) the log special fibre (𝒴̄, 𝒩̄) over (k, ℕ, 1 ↦ 0) is isomorphic, H_0-equivariantly, to the fibre of (Y, N) at T = 0; (b) Y is a projective H_0-equivariant blowup of u′T^{de}(∑X_i^N) = N∏X_i over W[T]′; (c) (Y, N) is log smooth over (W[T]′, ℕ, 1 ↦ T).
hypotheses: as in DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model
proofSteps: Both log special fibres are base changes of (Z, M) along S ↦ 0, U ↦ ū.
The charts of Z with U ↦ u′ give Kato charts of the form u′T = Z_1⋯Z_r, hence log smoothness (ComplexComparisonPartII C5 / CrystallineCohomology CR.5 log smoothness).
acceptance: For d = 1, e = 1 the lift is the reciprocal family itself near T = 0 with its semistable blowup.

nodes.title: Hyodo–Kato description of D_st of Dwork fibres near infinity
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite containing ζ_N, p odd and prime to N, λ|p, E/ℚ_p the λ-coefficient field, t∈F with v(t)>0, and F′,𝒴 as in DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model. Put K₀=W(k_{F′})[1/p] and V=V_{λ,t^{−1}}⊗E. The restriction V|G_{F′} is semistable and D_st,F′(V)=(B_st⊗_{ℚ_p}V)^{G_{F′}} is identified, H₀-equivariantly, with the χ-eigenpart of H^{N−2}_HK(𝒴̄,𝒩̄)⊗_{ℚ_p}E over K₀⊗E. After enlarging E to E′ and taking a label σ:K₀→E′, the character is transported by that coefficient map, equivalently σ^{−1}χ in fixed global coordinates. N preserves each component, while φ permutes them; φ^f is linear on a component for f=[k_{F′}:𝔽_p]. The filtration is compared only after scalar extension from K₀ to F′, using the Hyodo–Kato map determined by a uniformizer of F′. V is potentially semistable over F, with semistability asserted over F′.
hypotheses: p odd, p ∤ N
v(t) > 0 (Dwork parameter t^{−1} near ∞)
proofSteps: The C_st comparison for proper semistable models (CohomologyComparisons CP.4, with the actual Hyodo–Kato complex of CrystallineCohomology CR.6) is H_0-equivariant; take σ^{−1}∘χ-eigenparts.
The Hyodo–Kato cohomology of (𝒴̄, 𝒩̄) is that of the fibre at T = 0 of the log smooth lift (DM.8/log-special-fibre-witt-lift), which computes N as the residue of the Gauss–Manin connection.
acceptance: For the self-dual data with n = 2, N on D_st is nonzero, matching a multiplicative (Tate-curve-like) degeneration.

sources.locator: §4, definition of D_st,σ (foot of p. 20) and the first display on p. 21 (arXiv v1)

nodes.title: Regular ordinarity of Dwork fibres near infinity
nodes.statement: Let λ be a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2) of odd residue characteristic l ∤ N, F_v/ℚ_l finite containing ζ_N, Qian's datum (or the self-dual datum), and t ∈ F_v with v(t) < 0. Then: (1) there is a finite totally ramified F′_v/F_v with V_{λ,t}|_{G_{F′_v}} semistable, and for every σ the monodromy operator N on D_st,σ is maximally nilpotent (N^{n−1} ≠ 0); (2) V_{λ,t} is ordinary of regular weight μ with μ_{σ,i} = M(a_σ) for all i (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0); (3) ordinarity with the induced weights passes to G_{F_v}-stable subquotients, and hence for a G_F-stable filtration of a global V_{λ,t} (t ∈ F) each graded piece, and the semisimplification, is ordinary at v with Hodge–Tate weights the corresponding subset of {M(a_σ), …, M(a_σ) + n − 1}. Part (2) needs the consecutive labelled weights (the companion's Lemma 4.2 omits this hypothesis of BLGHT11 Lemma 2.2(2); PAPER-QIAN-23/E11).
hypotheses: l odd, l ∤ N
proofSteps: (1): DM.8/hyodo-kato-description-near-infinity gives semistability over F′_v and identifies N with the Hyodo–Kato monodromy of the σ^{−1}χ-part; maximal nilpotence follows from maximal unipotence of the complex monodromy at ∞ for the conjugate character σ^{−1}χ (DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity) through the comparison of the Hyodo–Kato monodromy with the residue of the Gauss–Manin connection.

Apply the already planned PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/maximal-monodromy-ordinary-criterion to the semistable restriction, using the consecutive filtration jumps proved in DM.7. That supplier explicitly allows a different starting value M(a_σ) at each embedding and uses the negatives as its own Hodge–Tate weights; its conclusion is precisely PL.0 regular ordinarity in the present convention.

(3): restricting the invariant full flag to a subrepresentation (or pushing it to a quotient) gives a full flag with a subset of the graded characters, whose weights remain strictly ordered; potential semistability passes to subquotients.

For descent to G_{F_v}, pass to a finite Galois extension where the representation is semistable. Its ordinary flag is the canonical flag reconstructed from ker N^j. The full Galois group preserves it because it sends N to a nonzero scalar multiple of N. The rank-one graded characters therefore descend, with the same labelled weights. Ordinarity is not inferred from arbitrary potential ordinarity.
acceptance: For the self-dual datum with n = 2 and v(t) < 0, V_{λ,t}((N − 3)/2) is an extension of ε^{−1}·(unramified) by an unramified character after a finite extension, like a Tate curve.

nodes.title: Regular ordinarity of Dwork motives near infinity for a general character
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite containing ζ_N, p odd, p ∤ N, and χ(ξ) = ∏ξ_i^{a_i} an arbitrary character of H_0 (∑a_i ≡ 0) with V_λ = e_χR^{N−2}π_*O_λ of rank n. Assume (a) for every σ ∈ Gal(ℚ(ζ_N)/ℚ) the monodromy of the σχ-eigen-local-system at t = ∞ has minimal polynomial (X − 1)^n, and (b) for every embedding the labelled Hodge–Tate weights of V_{λ,t^{−1}} are n consecutive integers. Then for every finite F_0/F and t ∈ F_0 with v(t) > 0, V_{λ,t^{−1}} is ordinary of some regular weight. Hypothesis (a) for all σ follows from the case σ = 1 by coefficient conjugation. The companion's sufficient condition 'a zero exponent gives (a)' is false (PAPER-QIAN-23/E50), and hypothesis (b) is not established for general χ there (E10).
hypotheses: (a) maximal unipotent monodromy at ∞ for every Galois conjugate σχ
(b) consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights
n≥1. The hypotheses are maximal monodromy for all coefficient conjugates and consecutive labelled filtration jumps; neither is replaced by the existence of a zero exponent.
proofSteps: As in DM.8/ordinary-near-infinity, using DM.8/hyodo-kato-description-near-infinity for χ and hypotheses (a), (b) in place of the computations for Qian's datum.
acceptance: For Qian's datum, (a) is DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity and (b) is DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights, recovering DM.8/ordinary-near-infinity.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2, p. 2; §4, pp. 19–23 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: The conditional main theorem of the companion, with the hypothesis of maximal unipotent monodromy for every σχ; Remark 1.2's zero-exponent criterion is false (E50).

nodes.title: Determinant twists, the module W and the torsor T_W for Qian's switch
nodes.statement: Hypotheses: l odd, n = l^a m (l ∤ m), s ≥ 1, N odd prime to ln with N > 100n + 100, r the order of l mod N with N ∤ l^{r/2} + 1 if r is even; F a CM field, M = F(ζ_N); r̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l^s}) continuous; λ | l a prime of O (of O^+ when n = 2) with k(λ) ⊇ 𝔽_{l²} and all m-th roots of elements of 𝔽_{l^s}; l′ > 2ln + 5 prime, unramified in F^avoid, l′ ≡ 1 mod N and l′ ≡ 1 mod n (PAPER-QIAN-23/E7, E36); λ′ | l′, k(λ′) = 𝔽_{l′}; r̄′ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_{l′}) with det r̄′ = ε̄_{l′}^{−n(n−1)/2} (local E9); finite Galois F^avoid ⊇ F, F_2^avoid, and totally real Galois F^suff over ℚ, all unramified above N, with F_2^avoid ∩ F^avoid = ℚ and F^suff ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = ℚ; F_0 = F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff(ζ_N). Construction: apply the finite-coefficient root theorem requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 to det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄|_{G_M})^{−1} (exponent m, DM.6/determinant-matching-at-l) avoiding F_0, getting L_1; then over L_1M to (det r̄′)^{−1} ⊗ det V[λ′] (exponent n, DM.6/determinant-matching-at-auxiliary-prime) avoiding F_0L_1, getting L_2 (two applications with the enlarged avoidance field, local E19). Put L = L_1L_2, E = LM. This gives (a) a totally real Galois L/ℚ linearly disjoint from F_0; the CM field E=LM is Galois over F; (b) characters χ̄_1 : G_E → k(λ)^×, χ̄_2 : G_E → 𝔽_{l′}^× with χ̄_1^n = det V[λ] ⊗ (det r̄)^{−1} and χ̄_2^n = det V[λ′] ⊗ (det r̄′)^{−1}; (c) W = (χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄) × (χ̄_2 ⊗ r̄′) over O/λλ′ ≅ k(λ) × 𝔽_{l′} with det W ≅ det V[λλ′], hence φ : ∧^nW ≅ ∧^nV[λλ′] and the torsor T_W = T({W}) over (T_0)_E (DM.5/level-structure-torsor); (d) T_W is smooth and geometrically irreducible (DM.5/level-structure-torsor-irreducible: l ≠ l′, max(l, l′) > 10, r′ = 1); (e) E ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff = F.
hypotheses: all hypotheses listed in the statement
proofSteps: The two root extractions are DM.6/determinant-matching-at-l and DM.6/determinant-matching-at-auxiliary-prime combined with the AGD R02.4 root theorem; the second application must avoid F_0L_1 so that L = L_1L_2 stays disjoint from F_0 (E37). The currently read AGD statement gives Q̄_l-valued roots only. Its requested strengthening must keep both roots in their fixed finite fields and keep the composite of the two totally real extensions disjoint from F₀.
Then det(χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄) = det V[λ] and det(χ̄_2 ⊗ r̄′) = det V[λ′], which gives φ by DM.5/determinant-descends.

(e): L and F_0 are linearly disjoint and M ⊂ F_0, so E ∩ F_0 = M; F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff is unramified above N, hence meets ℚ(ζ_N) in ℚ, so M ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff = F (tower disjointness, PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1).
acceptance: When r̄ already has determinant det V[λ]|_{G_F} and r̄′ has determinant det V[λ′], one may take L = ℚ and χ̄_1 = χ̄_2 = 1.

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, §4, root characters and construction of W, pp.22–23
sources.match: Constructs E = LM, the characters χ_1, χ_2, the module W and the isomorphism φ, and observes T_W is geometrically connected by Proposition 3.8, with the corrections E5–E7, E9, E36, E37.

nodes.title: Weil restriction of the torsor and the local valuation conditions
nodes.statement: With the switching data of DM.9/switching-determinant-data, let T = Res_{EF^suff/ℚ}(T_W ×_E EF^suff), a smooth geometrically irreducible ℚ-variety (Weil restriction along a finite separable extension preserves both properties), with the morphism p : T → Res_{EF^suff/ℚ} T_0 induced by T_W → (T_0)_E. Put Ω_∞ = T(ℝ) (nonempty since EF^suff is CM: T(ℝ) = ∏_{complex places} T_W(ℂ)), Ω_{l,0} = {(t_τ) : v_l(t_τ) < 0 for all τ : EF^suff → ℚ̄_l}, Ω_{l′,0} = {(t_τ) : v_{l′}(t_τ) > 0 for all τ}, and Ω_l = p^{−1}(Ω_{l,0}), Ω_{l′} = p^{−1}(Ω_{l′,0}). These are nonempty open subsets, invariant under Gal(ℚ̄_l/ℚ_l) (resp. Gal(ℚ̄_{l′}/ℚ_{l′})).
hypotheses: EF^suff a CM field
T_W smooth geometrically irreducible
proofSteps: Weil restriction of a quasi-projective smooth variety along a finite separable extension is a smooth quasi-projective variety, and becomes a product of conjugates over ℚ̄, hence geometrically irreducible (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.3; AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6).
t with v(t) < 0 (resp. > 0) avoids μ_N and ∞, so Ω_{l,0}, Ω_{l′,0} are nonempty open Galois-stable; p is finite étale and surjective on ℚ̄_l-points, so the preimages are nonempty open.
acceptance: If EF^suff has degree 2d over ℚ, then T(ℝ) is the product of d copies of T_W(ℂ), one for each complex place.

nodes.title: Qian's switching theorem for non-self-dual Dwork motives
nodes.statement: Keep the switching data of DM.9/switching-determinant-data. There are a finite totally real Galois L′/ℚ, linearly disjoint from F_0L over ℚ, and, with F′ = L′EF^suff, a point t ∈ T_0(F′) with a G_{F′}-equivariant isomorphism W ≅ V[λλ′]_t inducing φ_t on ∧^n, such that: (i) F′ ⊇ EF^suff is CM, finite Galois over F, with (F′)^+ = L′E^+F^suff; (ii) χ̄_1^{−1}V[λ]_t ≅ r̄|_{G_{F′}} and χ̄_2^{−1}V[λ′]_t ≅ r̄′|_{G_{F′}}; (iii) v(t) < 0 for every place v | l of F′ and v(t) > 0 for every v | l′; (iv) F′ ∩ F_2^avoid = ℚ and F′ ∩ F^avoid F_2^avoid = F, so F′ is linearly disjoint over F from every subextension of F^avoid F_2^avoid (in Qian's §4 these include F^av and F̄^{ker r̄}); (v) K = L′LF^suff(ζ_N) is finite Galois over ℚ with FK = F′ and K ∩ F^avoid = ℚ (the field that must be disjoint from F^avoid in the proof of Theorem 1.4; PAPER-QIAN-23/E3). Consequently V_{λ,t} has the prescribed residual representation at l, V_{λ′,t} at l′, V_{λ′,t} is ordinary at the places above l′ (DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point), and V_{λ′,t} has maximal unipotent (Steinberg-type) monodromy at the places above l (DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime). No automorphy statement is made here.
hypotheses: the hypotheses of DM.9/switching-determinant-data
proofSteps: Apply Moret-Bailly with three kinds of local conditions (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1) over ℚ to T = Res_{EF^suff/ℚ}T_W with S_1 = {∞}, S_2 = ∅, S_3 = {l, l′}, the opens of DM.9/weil-restricted-local-conditions and H = F_0L; ℚ is totally real with its real place in S_1, so the extension L′ is totally real.

A point of T over L′ is a point of T_W over L′EF^suff = F′ (L′ and EF^suff linearly disjoint), i.e. t ∈ T_0(F′) with an isomorphism W ≅ V[λλ′]_t respecting φ: this gives (ii) after untwisting by χ̄_i, and (iii) from the local conditions.
(iv) and (v) are intersection computations with tower disjointness (R23.1), using that L′ is disjoint from F_0L, L from F_0, and F^avoid F_2^avoid F^suff from ℚ(ζ_N).
The local consequences at l′ and l are DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point (l′ ≡ 1 mod N, v(t) > 0 means t ∈ 𝔪) and DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime (l′ ≠ l, v(t) < 0).
acceptance: For n = 2 the theorem reduces to the self-dual switch of BLGHT11 §6 with the real coefficient field, and its residual representations are symplectic.

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, §4, Proposition4.2 and intersection computations, pp.23–24; final proof of Theorem1.4, p.26
sources.match: Produces L′, F′ and t ∈ T_0(F′) with χ_1^{−1}V[λ]_t ≅ r̄|G_{F′}, χ_2^{−1}V[λ′]_t ≅ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{E,l′}|G_{F′}, v(t) < 0 above l and > 0 above l′, and the disjointness properties.

nodes.title: Switching in the self-dual Dwork family
nodes.statement: Let F/F_0 be a finite Galois extension of totally real fields, I a finite set, and for i ∈ I: n_i even, l_i odd primes, r̄_i : G_F → GSp_{n_i}(𝔽̄_{l_i}) with open kernel and multiplier ε̄_{l_i}^{1−n_i}; let l′ be an odd prime distinct from every l_i, with max(l_i,l′)>10 for every i and r̄′_i : G_F → GSp_{n_i}(𝔽_{l′}) with multiplier ε̄_{l′}^{1−n_i}, and F^avoid/F finite Galois. Choose N odd, prime to 2∏l_i·l′, N > n_i + 1, divisible by no prime ramified in F^avoid, such that each r̄_i takes values in GSp_{n_i}(Z[ζ_N]^+/λ_i) for a prime λ_i | l_i of ℤ[ζ_N]^+ (DM.1/auxiliary-modulus, BLGHT11 Lemma 6.1), and λ′ | l′. Then the product over Spec K, K=F(ζ_N)^+, of the symplectic level-structure torsors T_{r̄_i × r̄′_i} over their independent parameter lines (T_0)_K (isomorphisms compatible with the symplectic structures, BLGGT14's correction) is geometrically irreducible, and for an auxiliary finite Galois avoidance field L/K and a finite set Σ of finite places whose residue characteristics divide neither N nor l′, Moret-Bailly gives a totally real F′/F_0 Galois, linearly disjoint from F^avoid over F, and t_i ∈ T_0(F′) with: V_{n_i}[λ_i]((N − 1 − n_i)/2)_{t_i} ≅ r̄_i|_{G_{F′}} and V_{n_i}[λ′]((N − 1 − n_i)/2)_{t_i} ≅ r̄′_i|_{G_{F′}} as symplectic representations; v(t_i) < 0 at every place above l_i (and, in the variant of Newton–Thorne and Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, above Σ), v(t_i) > 0 at every place above l′. At such points: V_{λ′,t_i} is ordinary of weight 0 at the places above l′ (when l′ ≡ 1 mod N), has Hodge–Tate numbers {0, …, n_i − 1}, and at places above l_i (and Σ) the Weil–Deligne representation of V_{λ′,t_i} is an unramified twist of Steinberg.
hypotheses: n_i even; multipliers ε̄^{1−n_i}
N chosen as above; l′ ≡ 1 mod N for the ordinarity at l′

The base of the product torsor is (T₀)^I with one parameter t_i per factor. The avoidance condition is linear disjointness of field extensions over their stated base; it is not disjointness from a variety. The distinct-prime and >10 assumptions are the range of the product-monodromy node imported here.
proofSteps: For each i, full symplectic monodromy at the two distinct primes and DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy give a geometrically irreducible level torsor. Take their product over Spec K, with independent coordinates t_i; a product of geometrically irreducible K-varieties is geometrically irreducible. No assertion is made about a fibre product of all the torsors over one shared t.

Apply Moret-Bailly over a preliminary extension (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1, the corrected BLGHT11 Proposition 6.2 and BLGGT14 Proposition 3.1.1) with the local opens v(t) < 0 above l_i and Σ, v(t) > 0 above l′.
Local properties: DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point at l′, DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights, DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime at l_i and Σ.
acceptance: n_i = 2: the residual representations are GL_2 = GSp_2-valued with determinant ε̄^{−1}, and the switch produces a fibre that is Steinberg above l_i, the shape used by BLGGT14 Theorem 3.1.2.

sources.match: Chooses N by BLGHT11 Lemma 6.1, constructs the sheaves V_{n_i,λ_i}((N − 1 − n_i)/2) and the covers T_{r̄_i × r̄′_i} of BLGHT11 §4 (with isomorphisms respecting the symplectic structures), and finds a point by Proposition 3.1.1 with v(t) < 0 above l_i and v(t) > 0 above l′.
The self-dual Dwork family, its symplectic monodromy, local Galois properties of its fibres and the Moret-Bailly variant used to find points.

sources.locator: arXiv:2104.09761v1, rank-two convention after Proposition3.2, p.13
sources.match: Uses the self-dual family for n = 2.
Cohomological supersingular inertia uses negative fundamental-character exponents, and the auxiliary prime must be unramified in the avoidance field.

nodes.title: Local constancy of Galois representations in the Dwork family (Kisin)
nodes.statement: Let v | l be a place of a number field F ⊇ ℚ(ζ_N), λ | l a place of M, t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}) and an integer c≥1. There is an open ball U_t ∋ t in T_0(O_{F_v}) such that for all t′ ∈ U_t, W_{t,λ}/l^c ≅ W_{t′,λ}/l^c as representations of G_{F_v} (and likewise for finitely many λ simultaneously).
hypotheses: t integral with good reduction
proofSteps: Fix c≥1. The reduction of the lisse integral sheaf modulo l^c has finite fibres, and the sheaf of isomorphisms from its constant fibre at t is represented by a finite étale cover of T₀. That cover has an F_v-rational point above t.

A finite étale morphism is locally an analytic isomorphism on F_v-points at such a rational point, by the nonarchimedean inverse function theorem (equivalently Hensel’s lemma). Its image therefore contains an open ball about t; a lift of t′ is the required G_{F_v}-equivariant isomorphism of finite fibres. Intersect the finitely many balls for simultaneous places. This proves only fixed finite-level local constancy; it asserts no isomorphism of the full p-adic representations.
acceptance: If t ≡ t′ modulo a high power of the uniformiser, the reductions W̄_{t,λ} and W̄_{t′,λ} are isomorphic.

sources.locator: arXiv:2309.15880v3, proof of Theorem6.2.4, p.66; the roadmap uses its fixed finite-level consequence only
sources.match: Uses Kisin's local constancy theorem to find open balls on which W_{t,λ} mod p^c is constant.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.1, as cited by BCGNT25; original not read in this review (see sources and gaps)
sources.match: Secondary use or original-source pointer only. Local constancy in p-adic families of Galois representations.

nodes.title: Reductions of two-dimensional crystalline representations of small weight (Berger)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and r:G_{ℚ_p}→GL₂(E) crystalline, with E/ℚ_p finite and cohomological Hodge–Tate weights {0,m}, 1≤m≤p−1. Fix a stable lattice and read its reduction semisimply. Either r is ordinary, or up to an unramified character its reduction is Ind_{G_{ℚ_{p²}}}^{G_{ℚ_p}}(ω₂^{−m}); hence on G_{ℚ_{p²}} it is an unramified twist of ρ̄_{2,m,0}=ε̄₂^m⊕(ε̄′₂)^m, with the positive cohomological Lubin–Tate characters of L7/local-model-rho-nm0. In particular its inertia is θ₂^m⊕θ₂^{pm}, θ₂=ω₂⁻¹, and the induced reduction is irreducible. The inertia characters are extended to the unramified quadratic Galois group by the indicated Lubin–Tate normalization. An unramified twist and a finite coefficient enlargement put the nonordinary filtered φ-module into Berger’s displayed normalization.
proofSteps: Up to an unramified twist, the dual r∨ is Berger’s V_{k,a_p}, k=m+1: §1.3 defines D_cris(V_{k,a_p}∨)=D_{k,a_p}, with filtration jumps 0,k−1. The unit-root case v_p(a_p)=0 is ordinary (translate the rank-two supplier’s weight signs). In the nonordinary case a_p is in the maximal ideal. Theorem 3.2.1(1), pp. 277–278, applies for 2≤k≤p+1; here k≤p. It gives the semisimplified reduction of V_{k,a_p} as an induced ω₂^{k−1}, with its stated unramified normalization. Dualizing gives the exponent −m and possibly changes the unramified twist. Restrict to the quadratic unramified group and use the two conjugates θ₂,θ₂^p. Since 1≤m≤p−1, the exponent is not divisible by p+1, so this induction is irreducible.
acceptance: For H¹ of an elliptic curve with supersingular good reduction and m=1, the inertia is ω₂⁻¹⊕ω₂^{−p}, whose determinant is ε̄_p⁻¹. The Tate module has the dual, positive ω exponents.

sources.match: Splits the p-adic places into Σ^ord and Σ^ss using Berger's reduction theorem.
Berger states the reduction of V_{k,a_p} with D_cris of its dual equal to D_{k,a_p}. The cohomological application here uses that dual, k=m+1, and the negative fundamental-character powers.

nodes.title: Local Dwork points with prescribed reductions (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne)
nodes.statement: In the setting of the proof of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4 (primes p ≡ −1 mod N, r ≡ 1 mod N, p_0, q, places 𝔭, 𝔯, 𝔮 of M above p, r, q, a CM field F_4 = K^+F_3 with K^+_v large and the residual representations r̄_𝔭, r̄_𝔯, r̄_{CM,𝔯}, ρ̄_{A,q} trivial on G_{F_{4,v}} for v | prp_0q), for k ∈ {m, nm} and each such v there is a nonempty open _kΩ_v ⊂ T_0(O_{F_{4,v}}) of points t with: (i) v ∈ Σ^ord: _kW̄_{t,𝔭} trivial, _kW_{t,𝔭} crystalline ordinary, _kW̄_{t,𝔯}, _kW̄_{t,𝔮} trivial; (ii) v ∈ Σ^ss: _kW_{t,𝔭} crystalline and connected to ρ_{k,1,0} (the Fontaine–Laffaille representation ⊕ε_2^{k−i}(ε′_2)^{i−1}), residuals trivial; (iii) v | r: _kW_{t,𝔯} crystalline ordinary, residuals trivial; (iv) v | p_0: all residuals trivial; (v) v | q: _kW_{t,𝔮} crystalline ordinary, residuals trivial. Here _kW denotes the twisted Dwork system of rank k.
hypotheses: p > nm with p ≡ −1 mod N; r, q ≡ 1 or split as specified; F_4 chosen so residual representations are trivial locally

Use k>2 for the W-family: the m=2 modular-curve substitute is the separate rank-two target. Choose the preliminary local extensions first to contain an ordinary point, or the Fermat point with its component comparison, and to kill all finitely many residual representations. Then choose the global K⁺ realizing these local inclusions and avoiding B′; F₄=K⁺F₃. Local triviality of the four input residual systems alone is not claimed to imply all these extra conditions.
proofSteps: (i), (iii), (v): DM.7/generic-crystalline-ordinarity gives an ordinary crystalline point; Kisin's local constancy (DM.9/kisin-local-constancy) and the component lemmas for weight-zero crystalline lifts (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, BCGNT25 Lemmas 5.1.4–5.1.5) give an open ball of such points with trivial residual representations after enlarging F_4.

(ii): at t = 0, W_{0,𝔭} restricted to inertia is ⊕ω_τ^{i−1}ω_{cτ}^{k−i} (DM.7/fermat-fibre-inertia-at-minus-one), so its crystalline lifts connect to ρ_{k,1,0} (BCGNT25 Lemma 5.1.3, LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7); local constancy gives an open neighbourhood.
(iv): any point with trivial residual representations near t = 0 after enlarging F_4.
acceptance: For k = m = 2 the ordinary points of (i) correspond to ordinary crystalline rank-two representations with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}.

sources.locator: arXiv:2309.15880v3, proof of Theorem6.2.4, local data(i)–(v), pp.65–66

nodes.title: The CM-induced auxiliary system R_CM
nodes.statement: In the proof of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4: let F_1 be the Galois closure of FF_0, E/ℚ totally real cyclic of degree m disjoint from F_1 with p_0 unramified, L_1 = EF_1, q_1 an odd prime splitting completely in L_1 with v_1 | q_1 split as w_1⋯w_m in L_1. Choose an algebraic Hecke character Ψ_0 : 𝔸_{L_1}^× → M^× of the infinity type of Proposition 6.2.3(6a), unramified above the relevant set, with the restrictions Ψ_0|_{O^×_{L_{1,w_i}}} wildly ramified, pairwise distinct and of product 1; then (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4, BCGNT25 Lemma 5.3.3) a CM F_2/F_1 and a finite-order twist Ψ_2 of Ψ_0 ∘ N_{L_2/L_1} with det Ind Ψ_{2,λ} = ε^{−m(m−1)/2}. Then R_CM = {Ind_{G_{L_2}}^{G_{F_2}} Ψ_{2,λ}}_λ is a weakly compatible system of rank m, with Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, m − 1} and residual representations r̄_{CM,λ} absolutely irreducible on G_{F_2(ζ_N, ζ_r)} for the chosen r.
hypotheses: the infinity type of BCGNT25 Proposition 6.2.3(6a)

Keep F₂ linearly disjoint from the degree-m cyclic extension E and keep the determinant-correcting twist unramified at v₁. The chosen residual prime r differs from q₁, so reduction preserves the pairwise distinct wild q₁-power characters. N is unramified in L₂(ζ_r), which preserves the degree-m induction after restriction to F₂(ζ_N,ζ_r).
proofSteps: Existence of Ψ_0 with prescribed infinity type and local restrictions: algebraic Hecke characters with prescribed restrictions to finitely many local unit groups (HSBT10 Lemma 2.2 as restated in BLGGT14 Lemma A.2.4; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0).
The determinant correction by a finite-order twist after a CM base change is a root extraction of a finite-order character (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4).

Induction of a compatible system of characters is a compatible system (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5); distinctness of the local restrictions at w_i gives irreducibility of the residual induction.
acceptance: m = 1: R_CM is the character system of Ψ_2 itself.

nodes.title: Choice of primes and fields for the p–r switch
nodes.statement: Given R (the rank-two compatible system of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4 over F_2, with its set of good primes L(R)) and R_CM, there are primes N, p, r, q and fields with: N > 100nm + 100 prime, unramified in L_2 and M; p ≡ −1 mod N, r ≡ 1 mod N; p, r > 2nm + 1, p, r ∈ L(R|_{G_{F_2}}) prime to v_0v_1; p split in L_2 and M, r split in L_2(ζ_p) and M; Ψ_2 unramified above p and r; r̄_𝔭, r̄_𝔯 with image between SL_2 and GL_2; r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_2(ζ_N, ζ_r)}} absolutely irreducible; the p-adic places split into Σ^ord ∪ Σ^ss by DM.9/berger-reduction-small-weight; a solvable CM extension F₃/F₂(ζ_N), Galois over ℚ, linearly disjoint over F₂(ζ_N) from the field B cut out over F₂(ζ_N,ζ_p,ζ_r) by r̄_𝔭 × r̄_𝔯 × r̄_{CM,𝔯}; and, after adjoining e^{2πi/N} to M, a semistable elliptic curve A/ℚ with good reduction at p, r, p_0 and a prime q ∉ {p, r, p_0}, q > 2nm + 1, split in M, with ρ̄_{A,q}(G_{F_3}) = GL_2(𝔽_q) and A good ordinary at q.
hypotheses: the hypotheses of BCGNT25 Theorem 6.2.4
proofSteps: Primes p ≡ −1, r ≡ 1 mod N with the splitting conditions have positive density (Chebotarev); the excluded sets are finite or of density zero (big image for R at almost all primes).
Berger's theorem sorts the places above p.

A semistable non-CM elliptic curve over ℚ has surjective mod-q image for almost all q and is ordinary at a density-one set of primes (Serre); choose q accordingly, avoiding p, r, p_0 (as corrected in the extraction's review).
acceptance: p = 2N − 1 and r = 2N + 1 satisfy the congruences when they are prime.

nodes.title: The auxiliary Dwork systems R_aux and S_UA (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne)
nodes.statement: Let m > 2 and keep the data of DM.9/bcgnt-switching-primes and DM.9/bcgnt-local-dwork-points. (1) Applying Moret-Bailly with surjective specialisation (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1) to T(r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_4}}) (r ≡ 1 mod N, DM.5/level-structure-torsor), with f : π_1^ét(T) ↠ G the surjection onto the image G ⊆ GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) of the residual system W̄_𝔭 (G ⊇ SU_m(𝔽_{p²}), DM.5/residual-monodromy-su), F^avoid = B′F_4, S_0 = {p, r, p_0, q} and the opens _mΩ_v, gives a CM F_5 and t with R_aux = {W_{t,λ}}: r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5}) = G with multiplier ε̄^{1−m}, r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5(ζ_p)}) = SU_m(𝔽_{p²}), r̄_{aux,𝔯} ≅ r̄_{CM,𝔯}, and the local properties (i)–(v). (2) Applying it again to T(s̄_{aux,𝔭}, Sym^{nm−1}ρ̄_{A,q}|_{G_{F_5}}) for the rank-nm Dwork system, with F^avoid enlarged by the field cut out by r̄_{aux,𝔭}, gives F_6 and S_UA with s̄_{UA,𝔭} ≅ s̄_{aux,𝔭}, s̄_{UA,𝔮} ≅ Sym^{nm−1}ρ̄_{A,q} and the local properties (Hermitian structures being unique over finite fields). The printed claims r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5}) = GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) and F^avoid = B′F_5 are corrected as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/E29 and E32.
hypotheses: m > 2 (for m = 2 see DM.9/rank-two-auxiliary-system)
η compatible with the Hermitian pairings (local E26)
proofSteps: The torsors are smooth and geometrically irreducible (DM.5/level-structure-torsor-irreducible); the opens are nonempty (DM.9/bcgnt-local-dwork-points); the map f to the residual monodromy image is surjective on π_1^ét by definition of G as the full arithmetic image; its geometric subgroup contains SU_m.

Surjective specialization gives residual image exactly the actual quotient G. On G_{F₅(ζ_p)}, both the multiplier ε̄^{1−m} and determinant ε̄^{−m(m−1)/2} are trivial, so the image is contained in SU_m. Conversely SU_m is perfect in the stated range, and SU_m⊂G; commutators of lifts of its elements lie in G_{F₅(ζ_p)}, so SU_m⊂[G,G] lies in this restricted image. Thus equality holds. The multiplier alone need not have kernel SU_m, because x↦x^{1−m} on 𝔽_p× need not be injective.
The second application uses DM.0/hermitian-forms-unique to match the Hermitian structure of s̄_{aux,𝔭} with that of the rank-nm Dwork system.
acceptance: det r_aux = ε^{−m(m−1)/2} is compatible with the image G but not with GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) in full, which is why the printed equality is corrected.

nodes.title: The auxiliary system R_aux in rank two via twisted modular curves
nodes.statement: Let m = 2 in the setting of DM.9/bcgnt-auxiliary-dwork-systems. There are a CM field F_5/F_4, with F₅∩B′F₄=F₄, and an elliptic curve A_aux/F_5 such that R_aux = {H¹(A_aux)_λ} satisfies: H¹_ét(A_aux,𝔽_r) ≅ r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_5}} (symplectically); ρ̄_{A_aux,p}(G_{F_5(ζ_p)}) = SL_2(𝔽_p) = SU_2(𝔽_{p²}) up to the identification of SU_2 with SL_2; at v ∈ Σ^ss, ρ_{A_aux,p}|G_{F_{5,v}} connects to ρ_{2,1,0} (A_aux supersingular), at Σ^ord ordinary, at v | r ordinary, and the residual representations are trivial locally as in (i)–(v). The source omits this case ('a straightforward variant, left to the reader').
proofSteps: Use the twisted modular curve for the symplectic residual representation r̄_{CM,𝔯}∨, whose determinant is ε̄_r: the level structure is A[r]≅r̄_{CM,𝔯}∨, equivalently H¹_ét(A,𝔽_r)≅r̄_{CM,𝔯}. ModularCurves §5C constructs the fine smooth affine curve over ℚ and gives geometric irreducibility conditional on its connectedness contract. The CM-base version, that connectedness contract, and the universal elliptic curve must be supplied before applying Moret–Bailly here; they are recorded in the rank-two gap.

The remaining local construction must exhibit a nonempty neighbourhood on the twisted modular curve of a supersingular point whose lift connects to ρ_{2,1,0}, and ordinary neighbourhoods at the other prescribed places, after the finite local enlargements. Supersingularity of a chosen reduction alone does not prove the component comparison. This and the mod-p geometric monodromy statement are explicit proof inputs in the recorded rank-two gap, rather than consequences asserted from the existence of a CM point.

Moret-Bailly with surjective specialisation (R23.1), with f the mod-p monodromy of the universal curve, whose geometric image is SL_2(𝔽_p). Take the finite quotient G to be the actual arithmetic mod-p image of H¹ of the universal curve. Once the missing geometric SL₂-monodromy input is proved, commutators and the cyclotomic determinant give precisely SL₂ after restriction to G_{F₅(ζ_p)}; geometric monodromy alone does not say the full arithmetic quotient is SL₂.
acceptance: For m = 2, SU_2(𝔽_{p²}) ≅ SL_2(𝔽_p), so the image requirement is the familiar surjectivity onto SL_2(𝔽_p).
The level-r input uses the dual of the CM seed on A[r]. Its determinant is ε̄_r, whereas H¹ and the seed have determinant ε̄_r⁻¹; confusing them fails the Weil-pairing test.

sources.match: For m = 2 the auxiliary system is built from a modular curve with level-r structure instead of the Dwork family, and the details are left to the reader.

gaps.title: Hypergeometric convolution rank, local monodromy and determinant
gaps.detail: Katz90 Chapter 8 was not cleared or read. The exact specialized statements are checked in BCGNT §4.2, BLGHT Lemma 4.3 and Katz09 Theorem 5.3. The convolution construction is specified here, but proofs of its rank, irreducibility, purity, tame local monodromy and determinant require the Katz Chapter 8 arguments. Import the existing lower-shriek/base-change/trace contracts; do not count those imports as a proof of Katz’s theorem.

gaps.title: Finite classical-group classification, unitary generation and cross-characteristic orders
gaps.detail: The odd-characteristic n>2 transvection classification and restricted order comparisons are checked in their Qian/BLGHT/BCGNT applications, not against unread ZS76 and Artin55 originals. Supply the precise classification with exceptional cases, the unitary long-root generation/perfectness proof and the rank-two Dickson input used by BLGHT. A large-order element is not a substitute for checking the exception list. Handle Sp₂(𝔽₃) by its solvable composition factors, not by claiming it perfect.

gaps.title: Twisted modular-curve rank-two construction
gaps.detail: Current ModularCurves §5C supplies a fine curve over ℚ and only conditional geometric connectedness. Supply its CM-base version, the connectedness contract and universal elliptic curve with the required integral good reduction. Prove full geometric mod-p SL₂ monodromy and nonempty ordinary/supersingular component neighbourhoods after the prescribed finite local extensions. Use A[r]≅r̄_CM,r∨, equivalently H¹(A,𝔽_r)≅r̄_CM,r. Existence of a supersingular CM point alone does not establish the component comparison.

gaps.title: General-character ordinarity remains conditional
gaps.detail: Retain maximal nilpotence for every conjugate eigenspace and consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights as separate hypotheses. Qian21 Lemma 4.2 omits the latter (E10), and zero occurring in the exponent vector is not sufficient for maximal unipotence (E20). The selected zero-shaped data have the separate DM.4 and DM.7 proofs. No general limiting-mixed-Hodge argument supplying consecutive weights is asserted.

gaps.title: Equivariant correspondence comparison
gaps.detail: KM74 Theorem 2(1)–(2), pp. 76–77, was read directly. The rational Künneth projectors and algebraic-correspondence comparison must be exposed by RD.7 for the H-character projector, rather than inferred from its untwisted Frobenius statement. This gap concerns the supplier API, not unavailability of KM74 or Deligne §7.

gaps.title: Tame specialization and curvewise crystalline companions
gaps.detail: LPV.0–LPV.1 must supply the tame specialization formula near ∞, giving the nonzero valuation multiple of N∞ when v(t)<0 and residue characteristic is prime to N. DK17 §§5.1–5.3 transfer slopes by companions on smooth curves; they do not provide arbitrary-dimensional crystalline companions. Supply Abe’s curve companion input and the required full-faithfulness/restriction arguments in RD.2–RD.3; justify the choice of a curve meeting the needed open, since an arbitrary such intersection can be empty.

gaps.title: Recognition and coefficient control of the comparison character
gaps.detail: R24.5 owns the Hecke-character converse for algebraic/de Rham characters. Show the comparison characters satisfy its algebraicity and finite-ramification hypotheses without using DM.7, or state the precise compatible-character Henniart theorem used in BCGNT §4.2. The forward AG2.0 construction and compatible rational Frobenius values by themselves are insufficient. This is a supplier-hypothesis gap, not a new Hecke-character target.

gaps.title: Fixed finite coefficient field in root extraction
gaps.detail: The read R02.4 root statement permits values in an algebraic closure. Establish the stronger finite-field-valued root with the prescribed disjointness, or its primary-component variant; a root outside the chosen coefficient field does not define the required fixed-coefficient level torsor.

gaps.title: Equivariant toroidal subdivision
gaps.detail: SF.4 supplies strictly semistable schemes and alterations, but the needed equivariant unimodular subdivision after a ramified base change is an additional contract, requested there. General alteration existence does not prove an equivariant blowup preserving this generic fibre. Retain the extension degree e, and assert semistability over the resulting F′ rather than over F.

gaps.title: Nonarchimedean local inverse for a finite étale cover
gaps.detail: The fixed finite-level proof reduces to the local analytic inverse/Hensel statement at an F_v-rational point of a finite étale cover. Record this analytic contract explicitly in the supplier interface. Kisin’s stronger theorem is not used, and Berger’s §1.3 and Theorem 3.2.1 were read directly.

restructure.detail: The design brief asked this roadmap to build Qian's Lemma 2.1 (n-th roots of finite-field-valued characters after a totally real base change avoiding a given field, with its obstruction and two-primary steps). The accepted ArithmeticGaloisDuality packet already plans it: R02.4/character-root-obstruction (citing the proof of Qian's Lemma 2.1, pp. 1245–1247) and R02.4/character-roots-after-base-change (m-th roots of finite-order characters of a CM field after a totally real Galois extension disjoint from a given field), with R02.4/all-place-sha-duality for the Poitou–Tate step.
restructure.proposal: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 owns Lemma 2.1. This roadmap imports it in DM.6/determinant-matching-at-l, DM.6/determinant-matching-at-auxiliary-prime and DM.9/switching-determinant-data, after reducing (k^×)^n-valued characters to the prime-to-l exponent m and identifying k^× with μ_{#k−1} by Teichmüller lifting. No node of this roadmap plans the root extraction. The reviewed fixed-coefficient statement is stronger than the present algebraic-closure-valued root target: its finite-field form is explicitly requested, not silently identified with that target.

Qian's extraction places the same facts (its items 125–126) with the Dwork family, whose Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 3.8 use them.

They own the finite étale Galois category, arithmetic sequence, smooth/proper base change, adic realization, lower shriek and duality imported here. They are proposed roadmap targets, not implemented declarations or merged current-main content. The atlas snapshot has no stage IDs for this proposal. SF.2 in prerequisites and requests is only a graph adapter; upstreamContracts and upstreamImports identify each actual proposed owner. No proposed target is listed as a pinned declaration.

Read ComplexComparison Layers 8, 10, 12; EllAdicRealization Layers 8–10; and TraceFormula Layer 11 in open PR #196 at 4bd72379658126cbe9be935656396f0c9dac4de0. Import their comparison/trace targets, retaining pending status; no duplicate comparison theory is planned in DM. The same SF.2 graph adapter convention is used for these pending targets absent from the atlas snapshot.

At current upstream main 0d144d044dacebca17b654695b6f1ad58f159b27, §5C gives geometric irreducibility conditionally. Its connectedness contract, CM base, universal family good reduction, geometric SL₂ monodromy and local component inputs must be supplied for the rank-two Dwork application; no upstream files were edited.

Current README/Suggested contracts and current Tau Ceti a91d3aafa8cd3e6bc33dfde0d7677ed0f1625039 were inspected. Finite-field transvection classification and finite unitary generation are not supplied by characteristic-zero representation theory, a CFSG statement, or pro-p peripheral actions. Existing unitary and special unitary matrix carriers are reused from the pinned Mathlib; no upstream target is replanned.

upstreamImports.contract: Finite étale covers of a connected scheme correspond to finite continuous π₁-sets; finite lisse coefficient modules give continuous representations, and connected covers correspond to transitive actions. ECF §F.0.2.
For geometrically connected qc X/k, 1→π₁(X_kbar)→π₁(X)→G_k→1 is exact, with rational-point sections up to geometric conjugation. ECF §F.0.A2.
Proper base change for arbitrary torsion coefficients, compatible with coefficient maps, cup products and finite group actions. ECF §F.2.1.
Finite constructible cohomology for the stated finite-type/invertible coefficient regime; smooth proper lissity and fibre transport. ECF §F.3. This does not itself prove integral torsion-freeness.

Normalized integral adic realization and finite-E rational realization, with stable lattices, derived inverse-limit control and finite-dimensional proper cohomology; compatibility with base change, cup products and group actions. ECF §§F.4.1–F.4.6.

Smooth purity, trace and Poincaré pairings in the stated smooth proper invertible-coefficient domain. Integral perfectness here also uses the hypersurface torsion-free argument; EDC.2 explicitly retains the general Ext correction. ECF §F.6.
External tensor products, compact-support projection and Künneth, with the boundedness, finite-Tor and coefficient hypotheses used for the convolution. ECF §F.2.7.
Separated finite-type constructible lower shriek, base change, composition and compactification independence at finite levels, then normalized adic realization. ECF §§F.2.4–F.2.6 and F.4.

Finite ordinary and compact Artin comparison for complex algebraic schemes, plus proper relative Rf* and separated Rf! exchange on ctf inputs, compatible with cup products, finite groups and monodromy. CPC ComplexComparison Layers10 and12.
Pass finite Artin comparison to integral adic and finite-E rational realizations; keep the stable-lattice essential-image condition. CPC EllAdicRealization Layer10.

Grothendieck–Lefschetz for separated finite-type finite-field schemes with invertible finite ctf coefficients, and the rational corollary through adic realization; compatible with twists and finite group actions. CPC TraceFormula Layer11.
